news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Shohei Ohtani avoided surgery after his injury-plagued 2026 season.

Dodgers backup catcher Dalton Rushing, however, wasn’t so lucky.

Rushing was set to undergo an internal brace procedure on Wednesday to address the damaged ligament in his right throwing elbow, according to multiple sources with knowledge of the situation.

The operation will come with a nine-month timeline to return to full catching duties, as the Los Angeles Times first reported, but the expectation is that he could be ready as a hitter by the beginning of next season.

Rushing initially hurt his elbow at the beginning of August, while playing catch in the outfield before the start of a game. He spent much of the final two months of the regular season on the injured list, returning for only six days in early September before going down again when he suffered a setback in his throwing progression.

Rushing was healthy enough to be activated for hitting-only duties during the final week of the regular season. However, he did not make the team’s postseason roster, bypassed by rookie sensation Josue De Paula as the team’s left-handed bench bat in October.

Now, more uncertainty awaits Rushing, who is two years removed from his debut as one of the club’s top prospects.

For all the strides he took in his second MLB campaign –– batting .246 with 12 home runs and 36 RBIs in 80 games, including an extended stint in June and July as the fill-in starter behind the plate during Will Smith’s neck injury –– his place in the team’s long-term plans remains unclear.

Rushing’s surgery likely opens a pathway for Hunter Feduccia to begin next season in the backup catcher role, where he impressed as Rushing’s replacement down the stretch this year.

Where Rushing will fit into the early-season roster is unknown.

Though he could still offer an option off the bench with his bat, there might be few opportunities for regular playing time with Shohei Ohtani entrenched as the designated hitter and Freddie Freeman at first base.

It’s all just another setback for the 25-year-old slugger, who has yet to truly flourish at the big-league level.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Cornell Green, a five-time Pro Bowl and Super Bowl-winning Cowboys defensive back, died Wednesday, the team announced.

No cause of death was provided.

Green spent his entire 13-year career (1962-74) in Dallas, where he was part of the famed “Doomsday Defense” that led the team to prominence. The two-time All-Pro First Team member appeared in two Super Bowls, winning one in 1972.

“We are sad to share news of the passing of Cowboys Legend Cornell Green this morning,” the Cowboys said in a statement. Cornell was a true trailblazer having never played football in college, yet becoming a multi-time Pro Bowler, All Pro and NFL Super Bowl Champion with the Cowboys playing defensive back from 1962 to 1974. He was a member of the 25th Anniversary Cowboys Team as well. Cornell remarkably never missed a game in 13 seasons, becoming one of the best and most dependable teammates to ever wear the star. Our thoughts and prayers are with his family.”

Green played just one season of high school football and did not play college football, but was invited to the Cowboys’ training camp in 1962, after which he was offered a spot on the team.

He accepted the offer despite being drafted by the NBA’s Chicago Zephyrs earlier that year after he was a two-time All-American basketball player for Utah State, later being enshrined in the school’s Hall of Fame.

In his 13 seasons, Green did not miss a game, starting 167 of 168 contests. He led the Cowboys in interceptions four times and finished with 34 career interceptions, which ties him for fifth in team history.

Green played in two NFL Championship Games and Super Bowls V and VI, with the Cowboys defeating the Dolphins 24-3 in the latter.

Green retired after the 1974 season and later became a scout for the Cowboys and Broncos, earning AFC Scout of the Year honors in 2010.

For his efforts as a player, he was named to the Cowboys 25th Anniversary Team in 1984.

The push by Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer to investigate the lone holdout juror who forced a mistrial in her triple-murder case has been stopped in its tracks by the judge.

Clancy’s defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, had asked for an evidentiary hearing at an upcoming Nov. 2 court date to call witnesses to speak about accusations that Michael P. Desronvil lied on his jury questionnaire and used his cellphone during deliberations.

However, Judge William F. Sullivan wasn’t having it, and ruled Wednesday that the mistrial must only be evaluated based on the circumstances known at the time.

Additionally, Sullivan ruled that inquiring further into the juror’s reasoning or the jury’s internal deliberations would be inappropriate.

While Clancy’s motion to dismiss the charges remains pending, both sides are scheduled to present their arguments on Nov. 2.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

news.originalContent:
Manchester United winless run continues with 4-1 Champions League humbling in Como, and Bruno Fernandes slams tactics.

Manchester United captain Bruno ‌Fernandes said his side failed to apply enough pressure and adopted ⁠a “mood of defeat” ⁠after conceding early in Wednesday’s 4–1 Champions League loss at Como, a result that increased scrutiny on manager Michael Carrick.

Como opened the scoring ⁠in the second minute, and United collapsed, with only a stoppage-time consolation goal from Joshua Zirkzee making the scoreline slightly less severe.

“We started on the wrong ⁠foot, and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “There was not enough pressure on the ball and not many good movements off the ball. There were many things not going our way.

“It’s a decision from the [coaching] staff not to press man-to-man ‌and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

Asked if his comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me.

“Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and ⁠making them uncomfortable.”

Carrick has come under increasing pressure with ⁠United now winless in seven matches.

“It was more than disappointing,” the 45-year-old manager told TNT Sports. “I think everybody’s got to take responsibility for that. I’ll take responsibility for the overall team and performance; it stops with me, and I’m fine with that.

“But as a supporter of this football club, to see a ⁠performance like that is unacceptable, I have to ⁠say.”

Carrick said his side had failed to show the required intensity.

“It’s the motivation and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn’t bring that today,” ‌he said. “I’ve got to apologise for the performance.”

Fernandes also questioned United’s mentality after the early setback.

“Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood ‌of ‌defeat,” he said.

United have three points from their opening three Champions League matches and host AS Roma in their next fixture in the competition.

news.originalContent:
Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande score stunners as Real beat Leipzig to make it three from three in Champions League.

Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games, thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goalscorers for Jose Mourinho’s side.

Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range late in a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the advantage of the record 15-time European champions soon after the interval.

Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side, and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner late on to cap Madrid’s triumph.

Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona.

Without a major trophy in two seasons and after a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.

Mourinho started Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form.

The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla.

Visitors Leipzig created the first big chance, with Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois getting down low to make a superb save from Romulo Cardoso.

Vinicius, who improved on a poor showing at Roma last week without breaking out of his rut, drew a full-stretch save from Leipzig’s Maarten Vandevoordt.

Madrid carved out an advantage in the final stages of a low-key first half when Valverde cut the ball back for Guler, whose shot Vandevoordt saved. However, the goalkeeper could not clear it, and Silva darted in to prod over the line.

It was the former Manchester City midfielder’s first goal for the club after joining this summer.

Vandevoordt saved well from Valverde’s fierce effort before Guler put Madrid two goals ahead in the 52nd minute.

Jude Bellingham crossed to the back post and Mbappe nodded the ball across goal, with Guler able to hold off a defender and turn home.

Mbappe lashed a shot into the side netting after Bellingham teed it up, as Madrid looked to put the game out of sight.

Mourinho sent on Diomande for Vinicius with 20 minutes remaining, and the Brazilian looked disappointed on the bench, knowing he cannot play again until November 4, when Madrid visit AEK Athens.

Madrid’s record 140 million-euro ($157m) signing, Diomande, pulled the ball back to Mbappe on the edge of the box for Madrid’s third, and the French forward bent it home.

Leipzig quickly grabbed a consolation goal at the other end as Dean Huijsen switched off, with Gomis firing past Courtois.

Diomande ended proceedings with a bang, rattling an emphatic volley from Brahim Diaz’s cross into the top corner for his third goal in his last four appearances.

news.originalContent:
Eze gave Arsenal the lead, but Davies levelled and Kane netted a penalty for the hosts before Rice made it 2-2.

Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to grab last season’s runners-up Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal on Wednesday after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka, but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane.

Kane had Bayern on track for victory when he created and converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point.

Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout.

Despite the absences, Kane ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal’s miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London.

Kane’s second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid.

The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season.

Arsenal were hit with an early blow when Saka, their joint-top scorer this season, fell to the ground eight minutes in, grabbed his thigh and immediately signalled to the bench.

Bayern’s two previous Champions League opponents this term were from Norway, and the perennial Bundesliga winners seemed to struggle with Arsenal’s physicality as Mikel Arteta’s side pinned them back in the early stages.

With 25 minutes gone, Odegaard floated a simple pass across Bayern’s defence and into the path of the onrushing Eze, who collected and stroked the ball past Manuel Neuer.

Caught out by Eze’s perfectly timed run, the hosts looked even more surprised when VAR overturned the linesman’s offside call and awarded the goal.

The pre-match chatter had been dominated by talk of Kane’s Ballon d’Or prospects, and the England captain showed why he is among the favourites when he set up Davies’s equaliser 10 minutes later.

Kane spotted Davies on the move and threaded the ball through the midfield and around Gabriel for the Canadian winger to guide the ball into the bottom corner.

With the hosts now in the ascendancy, Ezri Konsa saw yellow for taking Kane out of a Bayern counter minutes later.

After the break, Neuer and David Raya took turns producing magnificent saves, with the Bayern captain tipping Bruno Guimaraes’s header onto the crossbar and the Spaniard denying Dayot Upamecano.

Both sides traded surges forward, but Kane would again prove crucial as Bayern took the lead.

Kane’s shot from the edge of the penalty area connected with Jurrien Timber’s arm, with the referee immediately pointing to the spot before Kane stepped up and buried his kick.

Bayern looked to be in control but the match turned again when late substitute Viktor Gyokeres threaded a clever pass to Rice, who slammed in an equaliser.

Kane told TNT Sports he was a little disappointed with the result.

“But probably when you look at the whole 90 minutes, a draw was probably a fair result,” he said.

news.originalContent:
The alleged participation of US agents in an April drug operation has raised questions about whether Mexican law was upheld.

Mexico has taken the rare step of charging a former state prosecutor with treason, alleging that he allowed United States agents to take part in a drug raid on the country’s territory.

The case underscores sensitivities about US involvement in Mexico and concerns about the Latin American country’s sovereignty.

On Wednesday, former Chihuahua Attorney General Cesar Jauregui was accused of permitting US agents to take part in an antidrug operation in the northwestern border state.

Under Mexican law, the federal government must approve the activities of foreign forces on the country’s soil.

But questions emerged about whether the law was being adhered to after two US agents and two Mexican law enforcement officials were killed in a car accident on April 19.

News outlets, citing anonymous sources, reported that the US agents had been collaborating with state law enforcement in the destruction of a drug lab.

Matias Gomez Leautaud, an analyst at the Eurasia Group, a US-based risk consultancy firm, told the news service Reuters that the treason charge “seeks to set a precedent and prevent cooperation between [Mexican] states and the US government without the federal government’s coordination and approval”.

While the administration of President Claudia Sheinbaum has collaborated with the US on issues of crime and insecurity, it has opposed any effort by the US to work directly with Mexican states without federal authorisation first.

In the days after the April car crash, Sheinbaum indicated that her government was not aware that US agents had been involved in a drug operation in Chihuahua.

“Evidently, the military didn’t know there were people participating who weren’t Mexican citizens,” Sheinbaum told reporters at the time.

She called for an investigation into whether state officials had respected Mexico’s constitution and its National Security Law, which govern the involvement of foreign forces on Mexican territory.

The constitution, for example, requires Senate approval for the presence of any foreign troops in Mexico. The country has a long history of US intervention, including multiple military invasions continuing into the early 20th century.

But concerns about the US respecting Mexican sovereignty have risen since US President Donald Trump returned to office for a second term.

Trump has suggested that the US could take unilateral military action in Mexico to address cartel drug-trafficking and violence, and he has characterised Mexico’s government as ineffective in addressing the problem.

“We have to eradicate them,” Trump said of the cartels in March. “We have to knock the hell out of them because they’re getting worse. They’re taking over their country. The cartels are running Mexico.”

In the aftermath of the April crash, conflicting reports emerged about why the two US agents were in the country.

Media identified them as members of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), a US foreign intelligence branch with a history of covert operations.

But state officials denied claims that they were involved in a drug bust. In a news release on April 20, Jauregui “ruled out the involvement of foreign personnel” in his state’s drug operations.

Instead, he said that US instructors had been present nearby for a training session about drones. They subsequently requested to join a convoy of Mexican law enforcement personnel to return to the airport, according to Jauregui.

“It is worth explaining what happened, in order to clarify the facts that are causing some confusion,” Jauregui said at the time.

He resigned from his post as state attorney general later that month.

Mexico’s federal Attorney General Ernestina Godoy has since accused Jauregui of permitting foreign agents to participate in operations on Mexican territory without first sharing information with federal officials.

A judge has ordered Jauregui to be held in pretrial detention as the court decides whether there is sufficient evidence to move forward with a criminal case.

Experts say the treason charge he faces is vaguely defined in Mexican law. It broadly covers acts that undermine Mexico’s sovereignty for the benefit of a foreign entity.

Convictions are rare, with the last widely recognised example coming in 1867, when Emperor Maximilian was tried by court-martial and subsequently executed for crimes against Mexico.

Jauregui is a member of the National Action Party, a conservative political movement in Mexico.  Sheinbaum, meanwhile, is a leader in the left-wing Morena party.

news.originalContent:
Race between sibling of former Senator Lindsey Graham, Democrat Annie Andrews has tightened in deep-red state.

United States President Donald Trump is set to travel to South Carolina to boost the campaign of Darline Graham, the sister of his close ally, the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

The visit on Wednesday, which will include a rally alongside Graham, comes as the Senate race in deep-red South Carolina has grown uncomfortably close for Republicans.

Lindsey Graham, long one of the most hawkish members of the Senate who was an outspoken supporter of the US-Israel war on Iran, had been expected to sail to victory in the November 3 vote. But his unexpected death in July upended the race.

South Carolina’s governor tapped Darline Graham to finish her brother’s term. Trump then made the surprise move of endorsing Graham in a new Republican primary, helping her to claim the party’s nomination. The president said the endorsement was “in honour of her brother”.

In a video message last week, Trump again said Graham had his unconditional support.

“I’m asking everyone in South Carolina to get out and vote for a wonderful person, a great woman … a woman that Lindsey Graham said is the greatest person he’s ever met,” Trump said.

Democratic challenger Annie Andrews, a medical doctor and paediatrician, has seized on Graham’s inexperience and her unorthodox route to the Republican nomination.

Speaking to a local Fox News affiliate before Trump’s rally in Pendleton, South Carolina, Andrews pointed to Graham’s lacklustre debate performance, including one instance where she said she was “not that informed on national security”.

“My opponent needs the highest level of federal government politicians to speak for her. On the debate stage, it was really clear,” Andrews said.

Graham, meanwhile, has called Andrews “the most radical liberal that’s ever run for state office in South Carolina”.

Polls have shown Graham leading by about 2.7 percentage points, according to a Real Clear Politics average. Trump carried the state by 18 percentage points in 2024.

Trump’s visit comes after the president issued an executive order waiving most sanctions and tariffs on Russia, established by a law named after Lindsey Graham and passed with bipartisan support in 2026.

The move prompted a tempered rebuke from Darline Graham.

“Personally, I would choose to put the ⁠pressure on Russia to end the war and get gas prices down,” she told The Associated Press news agency on Saturday.

“I don’t trust Putin, and I don’t trust Russia,” she said.

The executive order on sanctions has been part of a wider Trump administration shift in its approach to ending the war with Ukraine, which began with Russia’s invasion in February 2024.

Trump and his allies have heaped pressure on Ukraine, framing its leader, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, as the main impediment to peace. In turn, Washington has offered several concessions to Russia, including a deal to buy Russian diesel.

Lindsey Graham had been a staunch supporter of Ukraine. His death came shortly after he returned from his 10th visit to the country since the war began.

The tightening race in South Carolina underscores the harsh political reality for Republicans heading into the final stretch of the midterms.

Trump has sought to use his political clout to bring party loyalists out to vote, campaigning in strongholds across the country. But the president heads into the vote with the lowest approval ratings of his career, with voters expressing dismay about affordability and the knock-on effects of the US-Israel war with Iran.

Beyond South Carolina, other one-time Republican strongholds have shown signs of shifting towards Democrats.

That includes Kansas, where polls suggest Republican Ashley Hinson is effectively tied with Democrat Joshua Turek. The state, where farmers have been particularly hard hit by rising prices on fuel and equipment, has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1939.

Trump also broke from the Republican establishment to endorse Attorney General Ken Paxton over Senator John Cornyn in the Texas primary. Polling averages show Paxton, whose career has been marred by a procession of scandals, trailing behind Democratic challenger Talarico by 1.7 percentage points. The race is widely considered a toss-up.

A Republican has not won statewide office in Texas since 1994.

news.originalContent:
A jury found Meta guilty of lying to Facebook users in ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠New Mexico about access to their data.

A United States judge has ordered Meta to pay $25bn after a jury found the company misled Facebook users about privacy violations, marking the biggest fine ever against the tech giant.

New Mexico state District Judge Francis Mathew issued the ruling on Wednesday.

“Facebook promised users that they (the users) controlled their data. This was false,” he said.

Last month, a jury found Meta responsible for more than 43 million violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection laws. New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez highlighted that the decision was one of the largest state verdicts against a company in US history.

“This judgement should be a signal, an unambiguous message, to Silicon Valley,” Torrez said at a news conference.

Meta lawyer Matt Nicholson argued in court that a sum as high as $40bn would be “shocking to the conscience”, while a lawyer for New Mexico, Randi McGinn, urged standing up to “tech titans who think they are bulletproof and can do whatever they want”.

“The jury didn’t make findings that any New Mexican heard or saw these statements, or was harmed by them,” Nicholson argued during a hearing held early this month.

Torrez told reporters following the verdict that all the money awarded would go into a fund for the state’s education system.

The amount awarded in the case far exceeds the $5bn fine that the Federal Trade Commission levied against Facebook in 2019.

New Mexico accused Meta of misleading users about who could access their personal information and how harmful content was handled on its platforms. Jurors found that 26 of 29 statements made by Meta and its leadership on privacy and content moderation were misleading.

Meta plans to appeal the verdict, potentially reducing the final payment amount.

In a statement, CJ Mahoney, Meta’s chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal.

“This ruling, and the Attorney General’s approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Mahoney said. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online.”

The lawsuit, filed in 2021, stemmed partly from revelations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm that is now defunct, had obtained personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users without their consent and used it to develop targeted political advertisements. Its clients included President Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign.

The case, a major setback for the tech giant, marks the second legal defeat for Meta in New Mexico in six months. In March, a jury found the company misled users about the safety of young people on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, ordering it to pay $375m in civil penalties. Meta was later ordered to make an additional $567m payment into a state fund for teen mental health and was required to implement measures to protect young users.

Keon Ellis appears poised for a significant role with the Nets this season after an encouraging preseason showing.

The 26-year-old started all four of Brooklyn’s exhibition games, knocking down six 3-pointers despite playing no more than 24 minutes in any contest.

Ellis struggled in the preseason finale, but even that performance offered a positive sign.

Despite his shooting woes, he still attempted four shots from beyond the arc, suggesting he’ll have plenty of opportunities to let it fly this season.

And he’s certainly capable of taking advantage.

Ellis, who is better known for his defense on the wing, has been a reliable perimeter shooter throughout his career, connecting on more than 40 percent of his attempts from deep.

Last season, he averaged 1.3 threes per game, although that was only in 20.5 minutes per game while largely coming off the bench for the Kings and Cavaliers.

With his playing time potentially climbing closer to 30 minutes in Wednesday’s season opener against the Hornets at Barclays Center, Ellis should have more than enough opportunities to knock down at least two 3-pointers.

A year ago, the Nets were the worst shooting team in the NBA from beyond the arc, shooting a league-low 34 percent despite putting up 38.1 attempts per game.

Considering his track record and apparent role in Brooklyn’s offense, the over on his 1.5 made 3-pointers looks like a strong play to kick off the 2026-27 NBA season.

The play: Keon Ellis to make two or more 3-pointers (+105, FanDuel Sportsbook)

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The New Stanford Prison Experiment is a Netflix reality series that tries to recreate and improve upon the famous 1971 experiment where Stanford students volunteered to be either inmates or guards in a mock prison. But while that 14-day experiment failed after six days  as outside influence and other factors made things spiral out of control, the producers of this new version are trying to keep outside influence to a minimum.

Opening Shot: A view of a prison in Georgia. One of the participants in the series is asked if he’s ever been in prison before, and he says no.

The Gist: Thirty participants, including 3 women, selected from a cross-section of Americans, enter the prison in Georgia and are immediately split into two groups: 22 inmates and 8 guards. Three experts — behavioral psychologist Alison Wood Brooks, journalist Trymaine Lee, and corrections professional Michael Cantrell — watch the feeds of multiple robot cameras from a separate room and provide commentary.

During the first of the 14 days, most of the inmate participants want to go along to get along. But one participant, who spent a number of days behind bars during his younger years, starts stressing out over being back in that environment. Another inmate, who is a middle school teacher, vows to stir the pot by pulling pranks on the guards. And while the night shift guards are led by an entrepreneur who promotes trust and mutual respect, the day shift guards are led by an oil rig supervisor who feels that rules should be followed to the letter and punishments like lockdowns and being sent to solitary are absolutely necessary.

What Shows Will It Remind You Of? If you want to see a docuseries about the Stanford prison experiment, watch the Nat Geo series The Stanford Prison Experiment: Unlocking The Truth. The format of The New Stanford Prison Experiment reminds us of the reality series Unlocked: A Jail Experiment.

Our Take: One of the things that we kept saying to ourselves as we watched The New Stanford Prison Experiment was “These people volunteered to do this!” It was hard to put that out of our minds and just watch things play out. Given that there was no prize or anything else at the end of the experiment, we wondered why anyone would sign up to be locked up and be ordered around by a seemingly random group of people who just happen to be wearing different uniforms.

There are parts of this experiment that don’t quite jibe with the idea that there’s little to no outside influence, like the different tenors of the day shift and night shift guards. It just so happened that one group is led by a hard-ass and the other is led by a guy who seems like he’s playing improv games with the inmates? It feels too neat to us. And the one inmate who is there to foment chaos… why does he seem to be the only one? You’d think that if you volunteered to get locked up, you’d try some things, just to pass the time and make things interesting.

The New Stanford Prison Experiment is a Netflix reality series that tries to recreate and improve upon the famous 1971 experiment where Stanford students volunteered to be either inmates or guards in a mock prison. But while that 14-day experiment failed after six days  as outside influence and other factors made things spiral out of control, the producers of this new version are trying to keep outside influence to a minimum.

Opening Shot: A view of a prison in Georgia. One of the participants in the series is asked if he’s ever been in prison before, and he says no.

The Gist: Thirty participants, including 3 women, selected from a cross-section of Americans, enter the prison in Georgia and are immediately split into two groups: 22 inmates and 8 guards. Three experts — behavioral psychologist Alison Wood Brooks, journalist Trymaine Lee, and corrections professional Michael Cantrell — watch the feeds of multiple robot cameras from a separate room and provide commentary.

During the first of the 14 days, most of the inmate participants want to go along to get along. But one participant, who spent a number of days behind bars during his younger years, starts stressing out over being back in that environment. Another inmate, who is a middle school teacher, vows to stir the pot by pulling pranks on the guards. And while the night shift guards are led by an entrepreneur who promotes trust and mutual respect, the day shift guards are led by an oil rig supervisor who feels that rules should be followed to the letter and punishments like lockdowns and being sent to solitary are absolutely necessary.

What Shows Will It Remind You Of? If you want to see a docuseries about the Stanford prison experiment, watch the Nat Geo series The Stanford Prison Experiment: Unlocking The Truth. The format of The New Stanford Prison Experiment reminds us of the reality series Unlocked: A Jail Experiment.

Our Take: One of the things that we kept saying to ourselves as we watched The New Stanford Prison Experiment was “These people volunteered to do this!” It was hard to put that out of our minds and just watch things play out. Given that there was no prize or anything else at the end of the experiment, we wondered why anyone would sign up to be locked up and be ordered around by a seemingly random group of people who just happen to be wearing different uniforms.

There are parts of this experiment that don’t quite jibe with the idea that there’s little to no outside influence, like the different tenors of the day shift and night shift guards. It just so happened that one group is led by a hard-ass and the other is led by a guy who seems like he’s playing improv games with the inmates? It feels too neat to us. And the one inmate who is there to foment chaos… why does he seem to be the only one? You’d think that if you volunteered to get locked up, you’d try some things, just to pass the time and make things interesting.

But, aside from people like the retired cop who has a panic attack when his cell door is locked and the former juvenile delinquent who has bad flashbacks, it seems like everyone else just wants to “do their time,” which is really no fun on a show like this.

Parting Shot: In a side interview, the crap-stirring history teacher says he plans on getting inmates on his side and “take over this whole thing.”

Our Call: SKIP IT. We’re marginally interested in The New Stanford Prison Experiment in a “rubbernecking as we pass an accident” kind of way, but we’re going to be constantly watching and wondering why anyone in their right mind would volunteer to get locked up for no reason, and why the producers said they didn’t interfere when they so clearly did.

Liev Schreiber bizarrely got into a heated exchange with a red carpet reporter after he chastised her for trying to get a social media soundbite.

While at the New York City premiere of his new Apple TV show, “Nocturne,” Tuesday night, Schreiber’s back-and-forth with the reporter — who was part of Apple TV’s own in-house team — was caught on camera.

“Talk to people like you value what they do!” Schreiber told the woman.

He added, “It’s not a f–king soundbite, especially when we’re doing it in-house for our own people.”

He added that they’re trying to make the show “compelling” and advised her to “engage with the person.”

The “Ray Donovan” star, 59, then spoke about the question the reporter had asked him.

“That’s what they’re three words … three words are not gonna do anything to anybody, and the monkey that f–king thought of that is shooting themselves in the foot,” he said.

“If you wanna give them something that they can use, talk to people like they’re humans, not like it’s social media,” the Tony Award winner added.

The reporter handles the scolding well, keeping a smile on her face during most of the discussion and appearing to nod in agreement with what Schreiber was saying.

He then waved the cameraman to come back over to film and things appeared to end amicably.

The Con Edison worker killed in a road rage-fueled shooting on the George Washington Bridge late Tuesday was a hardworking “family man” who “had so much life,” kin said Wednesday.

Dad-of-two Koran Irvine, 46, was on his way home from an overtime shift with the energy company when hetook a bullet to the right shoulder around 7:15 p.m. Tuesday on the New Jersey-bound upper level of the crossing, according to cops and his family.

“He’s a family man. Has always been a family man, and he lived his life 100% for his family, stayed out of trouble. And I am in disbelief at this point in time,” a cousin told The Post.

“He was a man that lived for his family 100%, the only thing that he loved near and dear to his heart as much as his family was the Jets.”

Irvine, of Valley Cottage, Rockland County, had a son and a daughter – and loved ones admired his relationship with his wife.

“From just their dynamic and how you would experience it in person, you just felt that love in the air,” one relative said. “They really loved each other. They were a special couple.”

“The kids too, they loved their dad and it’s not too long ago they celebrated his birthday.”

Irvine was also a “jokester” who “just always wanted to make people laugh and feel good,” kin said.

“He is always the light of the party,” the relative added. “He had so much life, was very attentive to everyone, always wanted to know people’s needs. He was so inviting.”

He recently lost his mother, but carried the grief with grace, according to the family member.

“Even when his mom passed away a few years ago, he was obviously going through a difficult time, but never made it about himself,” the relative said.

A person of interest surrendered to cops less than 24 hours after the deadly violence and was being questioned Wednesday afternoon, the sources said.

Couples moving in together can be a rough adjustment. But an Instagram post Tanner made on Tuesday suggests that Clark has passed with flying colors, at least when it comes to bathroom etiquette.

In the video, Tanner spoke about the “bathroom green flags” that men should keep in mind if they’re about to be moving in with or already living with their girlfriend.

The first one she mentioned was a good-smelling candle. Then she said a good grooming tool is important. After that, she conveyed the important of clean, white towels.

“This one might be super niche, but a good hand soap. Because when I’m doing my makeup and then washing my hands after, I don’t want to get my makeup on my white towels,” Tanner said before adding lotion and mouthwash as other green flags.

“And then, obviously, the basics of keeping your bathroom clean, [and] not having hair everywhere,” Tanner mentioned as her final piece of advice.

Clark’s adherence to these “green flags” is likely one reason why he and Tanner appeared on the verge of getting engaged, even though Clark hasn’t popped the question quite yet.

news.originalContent:
Olfa ⁠Hamdi, a US-Tunisian national, was convicted of ‘plotting’ and ‘inciting’ military to disobey orders.

A Tunisian military court has sentenced an opposition ⁠leader to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the ⁠military to disobey orders, her lawyer has said.

The charges against Olfa ⁠Hamdi, a dual Tunisian and United States national, stemmed from social media posts, her lawyer Akram Moussa said on Wednesday. Hamdi has repeatedly criticised Tunisian President Kais Saied’s rule and called for a transitional government and early presidential elections.

Critics say the case against Hamdi is the latest in a crackdown on opponents of Saied.

In Tunisia’s 2024 elections, Hamdi, who was then 36, sought to run for president. Her candidacy was rejected for not meeting the 40-year age minimum for candidates.

Hamdi, the leader of the Third Republic Party, was detained at Tunisia’s main airport after disembarking from a flight in February.

She ‌had been living abroad, running a consulting firm in the US after briefly serving as the head of Tunisia’s national airline Tunisair.

Hamdi’s sentence comprises two separate two-year prison terms from two additional convictions and 80,000 dinars ($26,000) in fines, her lawyer said.

Hamdi was also sentenced in March in a separate case to two years in prison. Global human rights organisations have widely criticised the cases against her.

A US Department of State spokesperson told the AFP news agency that Washington was “closely tracking the situation”.

“The [President Donald] Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of American citizens,” he said.

Rights groups have criticised Saied, accusing him of rolling back freedoms in a 2021 power grab.

Thousands of ‌Tunisians joined the largest protest against Saied in years on Saturday, accusing him of undermining democracy and ‌mishandling ‌the economy. Opposition leaders, activists ⁠and journalists have been imprisoned during his rule.

Saied rejects accusations that he is targeting political opponents and critics, saying the law applies to everyone regardless of their position.

Olfa ⁠Hamdi, a US-Tunisian national, was convicted of ‘plotting’ and ‘inciting’ military to disobey orders.

A Tunisian military court has sentenced an opposition ⁠leader to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the ⁠military to disobey orders, her lawyer has said.

The charges against Olfa ⁠Hamdi, a dual Tunisian and United States national, stemmed from social media posts, her lawyer Akram Moussa said on Wednesday. Hamdi has repeatedly criticised Tunisian President Kais Saied’s rule and called for a transitional government and early presidential elections.

Critics say the case against Hamdi is the latest in a crackdown on opponents of Saied.

In Tunisia’s 2024 elections, Hamdi, who was then 36, sought to run for president. Her candidacy was rejected for not meeting the 40-year age minimum for candidates.

Hamdi, the leader of the Third Republic Party, was detained at Tunisia’s main airport after disembarking from a flight in February.

She ‌had been living abroad, running a consulting firm in the US after briefly serving as the head of Tunisia’s national airline Tunisair.

Hamdi’s sentence comprises two separate two-year prison terms from two additional convictions and 80,000 dinars ($26,000) in fines, her lawyer said.

Hamdi was also sentenced in March in a separate case to two years in prison. Global human rights organisations have widely criticised the cases against her.

A US Department of State spokesperson told the AFP news agency that Washington was “closely tracking the situation”.

“The [President Donald] Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of American citizens,” he said.

Rights groups have criticised Saied, accusing him of rolling back freedoms in a 2021 power grab.

Thousands of ‌Tunisians joined the largest protest against Saied in years on Saturday, accusing him of undermining democracy and ‌mishandling ‌the economy. Opposition leaders, activists ⁠and journalists have been imprisoned during his rule.

Saied rejects accusations that he is targeting political opponents and critics, saying the law applies to everyone regardless of their position.

news.originalContent:
Tehran had ‘nothing new’ to tell Washington after latest nuclear proposals reportedly offered by mediators.

Tehran, Iran – There has been a flurry of diplomatic activity in the Middle East in recent days, with hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough to end the United States and Israel war on Iran.

Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir was in Tehran on Wednesday to discuss the war and recent tensions in Yemen. It comes against the backdrop of fears of a new breakout in conflict in the region.

Despite this, Tehran has held firm to its position that the war will not end, and the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen, until the US accepts its conditions.

Iran maintains an unyielding stance on its contentious nuclear programme, which was a factor in the Trump administration’s decision to launch the war on February 28.

“Not a single gram of enriched uranium will be removed from Iran,” Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said late Tuesday after meeting Munir.

But he did not rule out downblending the highly enriched uranium inside the country under supervision from monitors, something Iran has offered before.

Iran’s authorities present the decades-old nuclear programme as a sovereign right and an achievement gained despite strikes, sabotage and assassinations. Rezaei described it as “national wealth” on Tuesday.

Iran has also used low-enriched uranium for civilian purposes like manufacturing radiopharmaceuticals and for power generation at the Bushehr plant in cooperation with Russia.

The authorities argue that surrendering the nuclear programme under military pressure would amount to capitulation, if it did not guarantee that Iran would not be left exposed to more attacks.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly emphasised since the start of the war that he wanted to dismantle the Iranian nuclear programme. US Vice President JD Vance, however, suggested earlier this month that a “meaningful” reduction in the level of enrichment capacity may satisfy US demands.

Before Israeli and US attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities in June 2025, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) estimated that Tehran possessed 440 kilogrammes (970 pounds) of uranium enriched up to 60 percent. A nuclear bomb would need enrichment of more than 90 percent.

The attacks, followed by further US-Israeli strikes on nuclear sites in 2026, severely damaged Iran’s nuclear infrastructure. With the IAEA unable to inspect key facilities, the current size, condition and whereabouts of much of Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile remain unverified.

Tehran has refused access to the IAEA to inspect its nuclear facilities since the war started, accusing the agency of advancing Western interests through adopting resolutions and referring the nuclear file to the United Nations Security Council.

Iranian authorities maintain they are not pursuing a bomb. But senior Iranian officials, like Rezaei, have publicly questioned the validity of being a party to the international nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty if Iran’s nuclear facilities and other infrastructure continue to be attacked.

Still, Iranian officials have hosted numerous foreign diplomats this week. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov was in Tehran on Monday after attending a meeting with Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries a day earlier. There were also indications of visits to Tehran by other Arab officials.

US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is also reported to have met Israeli security officials earlier this week. These meetings did not appear to have decreased the prospects of renewed war.

But speaking at a conference for Iranian exporters in Tehran on Wednesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi cautioned that the country faces threats of more attacks and expansive economic sanctions.

“The reality is that the country is truly in war conditions and the war continues. We have not reached peace conditions and are away from it, so all decisions must be made within war conditions,” he said.

Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told Munir that Iran had “nothing new” to tell Washington and expected realisation of conditions offered in New York last month to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.

Mediators did not publicly divulge details of their proposals to Tehran this week, but were told the US needed to build trust by accepting Iran’s conditions. These include returning to the June memorandum of understanding and recognising an Iran-Oman deal over temporary transit in the Strait of Hormuz.

In addition to a pledge for immediate talks on a bigger deal regarding Iran’s nuclear issue, the memorandum included removing the US naval blockade on southern Iranian ports, waivers for oil sanctions, unfreezing Iranian assets and halting military action in Lebanon and other regional hotspots.

Ellie Geranmayeh, a senior policy fellow and deputy head of the Middle East and North Africa programme at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said it was clear that Tehran would be unwilling to give up its enriched uranium without guarantees of sanctions relief.

“The Iranians have made it very clear, and I see no evidence that’s changing, that they are willing to negotiate over the fate of the highly enriched uranium or access for international monitors, but that has to be directly linked with a very clear implementation protocol for US sanctions relief,” she told Al Jazeera. “We are very far from those types of negotiations at this stage.”

US media cited unnamed officials as saying on Tuesday that the Pentagon was sending the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and a Marine unit to the Middle East. That would present President Trump with a range of strike options after the US midterm elections on November 3.

Over recent weeks, Trump and his officials have further discussed a range of military operations, including hitting Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain to diminish nuclear facilities inside, and dropping the “mother of all bombs” on nuclear and energy facilities. They have also previously raised the idea of seizing Iran’s southern islands on the Strait of Hormuz and assassinating more Iranian officials.

Iran’s state-run Press TV cited an unnamed security official as saying on Wednesday that decision-makers in Tehran have chosen to advance “without any limitations or restraint” if there are more US and Israeli attacks or assassinations.

Geranmayeh pointed out that Tehran had also helped its ally, the Houthis in Yemen, with their advances along the Bab al-Mandeb strait, and even considered potential preemptive strikes to rattle the US ahead of the election.

“One thing we should be watching out for is Israel and the US combining forces on military attacks after the Israeli elections and the US midterms,” she said, after Trump backed Netanyahu’s election bid.

news.originalContent:
Public sector workers and teachers joined student protesters, amid growing youth-led demonstrations across Europe.

Milan’s youth follow France in violent cost-of-living protests

Thousands of students and teachers ‌have rallied across cities in Greece, demanding more funding for ⁠education, including better facilities and smaller ⁠class sizes.

The demonstrations echo a wave of youth-led protests across Europe this month, including in France and Albania, where anger over rising costs and alleged corruption has led to clashes with police and major property damage.

Greek police said about 10,000 demonstrators, including school and university students, rallied peacefully in central Athens and the capital’s suburbs on Wednesday.

“From Greece to France, we want public, free education,” protesters chanted as they gathered outside Parliament, where students staged an overnight sit-in nearby before the rally.

Others joined the protests in Thessaloniki, Patras, Larissa and other cities ⁠across Greece in solidarity with growing demonstrations in France and elsewhere in Europe, where rallies demanding educational resources have morphed into angry demonstrations over soaring living costs.

In Greece, the protests add pressure to ⁠Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and his centre-right government as the country prepares to hold elections in mid-2027 amid a weakening economy.

Greece struggled with a serious debt crisis from 2009 to 2018, during which the government agreed to spending cuts in exchange for three European Union and International Monetary Fund bailouts worth about 290 billion euros ($326bn).

But the measures have impacted Greek workers, who are among the poorest in Europe and struggle with stagnant wages, high rents and rising energy costs.

The average monthly salary of 1,500 euros ($1,685) sits at 2009 levels, with many young Greeks having been priced out of housing in ⁠cities by skyrocketing rents.

“Surviving here is very difficult; the ⁠rent is really high, the houses are really small. Our parents can’t make ends meet to pay for our rent, the electricity, for our life here,” university student Georgia Foukidou, 21, who joined the protest in Athens, told the Reuters news agency.

The protests on Wednesday included strikes by primary and secondary school teachers protesting low pay and staff shortages, while substitute teachers demanded permanent positions and reduced class sizes. Public sector workers and other unions also joined the demonstrations.

Education Minister Sofia Zacharaki said prior to the protests that she was listening to student demands, noting that the government was spending more than 733 million euros ($823m) on new student residences and facilities upgrades.

Mitsotakis’ government has also pledged about one billion euros ($1.12bn) in state subsidies and other benefits to offset increased energy costs for households and businesses due to the Iran war and inflation.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Angelina Katsanis/Getty Images)

Cathy Engelbert, the commissioner of the WNBA, told Republican lawmakers that ex-NBA stars Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White are not eligible to compete in the league because they’re “both men.”

Engelbert’s comments came in a response to a congressional inquiry, but she did not provide the definition of “women” that lawmakers requested.

“With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men,” wrote Engelbert in the response dated Oct. 16. (RELATED: Steelers-Saints Game In Paris Still On Despite Riots, NFL Says)

The America First Policy Institute (AFPI), representing Freedom, provided the letter to OutKick.

The letter was a response to an inquiry, dated Sept. 17, from GOP Rep. Marlin Stutzman of Indiana and four other House Republicans regarding eligibility, safety for players, and fan confrontations.

Both Freedom and White have claimed to identify as women and have announced that they intend to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft.

🚨 OUTKICK EXCLUSIVE: The WNBA suddenly knows what a woman is? @EnesFreedom announces in an interview with @JackThompsonFOX that the WNBA sent a letter yesterday declaring him and @Highway_30 ineligible for the WNBA Draft because both are men. https://t.co/oqtRm1OXBj

The lawmakers questioned what the WNBA’s definition of “women” is under Article XIII, Section 1(a) of the league’s collective bargaining agreement and why Freedom and White were denied eligibility.

“Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA,” the provision of the 2026 agreement states. It does not define the term.

Stutzman welcomed Englebert’s statement as an acknowledgement of a biological sex distinction.

“The WNBA has just taken the first step in defining what a woman is for the sports community,” he said in a statement.

“By clearly labeling Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White as men they have acknowledged that identifying as a woman does not change basic human biology.”

🚨 OUTKICK EXCLUSIVE: The WNBA suddenly knows what a woman is? @EnesFreedom announces in an interview with @JackThompsonFOX that the WNBA sent a letter yesterday declaring him and @Highway_30 ineligible for the WNBA Draft because both are men. https://t.co/oqtRm1OXBj

The lawmakers questioned what the WNBA’s definition of “women” is under Article XIII, Section 1(a) of the league’s collective bargaining agreement and why Freedom and White were denied eligibility.

“Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA,” the provision of the 2026 agreement states. It does not define the term.

Stutzman welcomed Englebert’s statement as an acknowledgement of a biological sex distinction.

“The WNBA has just taken the first step in defining what a woman is for the sports community,” he said in a statement.

“By clearly labeling Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White as men they have acknowledged that identifying as a woman does not change basic human biology.”

In his first comments since the Yankees lost to the Rays in an ALDS sweep, Yankees owner Hal Steinbrenner cited the offense as one of the reasons for yet another early postseason exit for the Bombers.

Steinbrenner was asked what changes the Yankees have to make to “get over the hump.”

“I was disappointed, frankly, with the offense throughout the course of the year as a whole,” Steinbrenner said Wednesday morning.

“As a whole, they were very inconsistent and for long periods of time. This has been twice now where the offense hasn’t lived up to their end of the bargain and got the job done. The offense was a big disappointment for me and it has to be better.”

Steinbrenner went so far as to call the Yankee offense “detrimental.”

He admitted that losing star sluggers Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton for over 80 games certainly affected them — with Judge not playing in the postseason — but he stated that he and the Yankees will be evaluating everything “from the top” when figuring out where their offseason priorities lie.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Aday Mara needed just one game to suddenly make the Thunder seem much better suited to handle Victor Wembanyama this season.

The Thunder’s 7-foot-3 rookie had a strong debut Tuesday and helped Oklahoma City hold the Spurs’ phenom to a career-worst shooting night in a 116-104 road win in a Western Conference finals rematch.

Mara scored seven points while adding two rebounds and one block in 12 minutes, including a pivotal third-quarter sequence where he blocked Wembanyama and then scored on the other end.

OKC really drafted the Wemby stopper 😭Mara just OWNED Wemby on BOTH ends pic.twitter.com/jtXIMwcS8m

“He was awesome,” Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said. “Great poise, great impact. He had probably one of the stretches of the game — it’s a critical thing there when he blocked the shot and went down and finished the other end. He didn’t seem overwhelmed by the atmosphere of the game.

“I’m not really surprised by how he’s performed in preseason. I think he’s proven to be a very impactful player. His minutes weren’t high tonight but his impact was. Clearly, somebody we trust, put him in that game and we’re only going to trust him more after seeing how he performed in a high-level game.”

The Thunder and Spurs are both stocked with talent and seem destined to clash in the playoffs for years to come, meaning they both can build rosters with the other team in mind.

In last year’s conference finals, Wembanyama had his way against Oklahoma City to the tune of 27.3 points per game, 10.9 rebounds per contest and 2.7 blocks per game to eliminate the reigning champions.

Oklahoma City’s big-man duo of Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein proved helpless in the series, with Holmgren particularly being ineffective.

The Thunder responded by using the No. 12 pick in the draft to select Mara out of Michigan after he helped the Wolverines win the national title.

Adding the 262-pounder suddenly gave Oklahoma City another weapon to throw at Wembanayama, and he provided encouraging results Tuesday.

His highlight sequence came in the third quarter with Oklahoma City leading 82-70 when Mara blocked Wembanyama while he attempted to score on an alley-oop.

Moments later, Mara scored on an alley-oop.

Mara told a Spanish outlet that he received a game ball for his efforts.

“I’m happy it’s official now,” he told CARTV, as reported by eurohoops.net. “I felt good playing, and I felt like I helped the team, so I’m happy.”

The trio of Mara, Holmgren and Hartenstein ultimately held Wembanyama to 13 points on 1 of 12 shooting to allow the Thunder to exact revenge for last year’s playoffs exit.

“There’s always a variance to it,” Daigneault said of slowing down Wembanyama. “I thought he missed shots that he can normally make from the floor. I thought Chet did a great job on him. I thought Mara did a great job on him the possessions he had tonight.

“I thought we collectively had the right amount of response to him.”

You’ve seen it before — the skincare commercial where someone joyfully splashes water on their face, usually right before the screen flashes the words “hyaluronic acid” in bold.

That signature water imagery? It’s not just for show. It perfectly captures what the best hyaluronic acid serums are designed to do: hydrate, plump and refresh your skin like a tall glass of water for your face.

So, what is hyaluronic acid, really? Despite the slightly intimidating name, it’s not a harsh chemical. In fact, it’s a naturally occurring substance found in your skin, joints and eyes. As a powerful humectant, hyaluronic acid draws moisture from the environment and locks it into your skin — making it an essential ingredient in many moisturizers, serums and even lip balms. The result? Smooth, supple skin that looks healthier and more hydrated.

Whether you’re wondering how to use hyaluronic acid, whether hyaluronic acid causes acne, or how it compares to niacinamide, there’s no denying the ingredient’s versatility. It’s loved by dermatologists and skincare lovers alike, and the benefits of hyaluronic acid go far beyond hydration (think: improved skin texture, minimized fine lines and even soothing support for sensitive or acne-prone skin).

To help you navigate the best options on the market, we’ve rounded up top-rated products — from the best overall hyaluronic acid serum to a gentle lip balm, nighttime serum and more. No matter your skin type or concern, there’s a hyaluronic acid solution for you.

“Hyaluronic acid is a natural substance found in our skin that helps keep it moisturized and plump,” Rachel Nazarian, MD, board-certified dermatologist at Schweiger Dermatology Group in NYC, told the New York Post. “Because of its ability to draw and hold water, it’s referred to as a ‘humectant moisturizer’ — and keeps skin moisturized throughout the day, [minimizing] the appearance of fine lines and superficial wrinkles.”

Ahead, find the alluring, barrier-repairing serums, face masks, lip balms, and lotions that’ll bring your skin back to life (when used consistently, that is). Once you begin dousing your face and body with HA, you’ll be in for a dewy, glowing-from-within treat.

The Drunk Elephant B-Hydra Intensive Hydration Serum is an incredibly moisturizing, humectant-forward serum that wears many hats in its formulation. For one, it helps minimize the look of fine lines, helps reverse and alleviate the impact of my dry, flaky skin and essentially floods my skin with nourishment. It’s the crème de la crème of hyaluronic acid serums, namely for its ability to mask away dullness and conquer even the driest of regions on the face.

Leave it to me — I’ve reviewed all of Drunk Elephant and the brand goes beyond its photo-worthy matte white lotions and potions with a fun, neon cap. The magic is what lies inside and, in this case, it’s hydration.

Drunk Elephant’s B-Hydra Intensive Hydration Serum is packed with pineapple ceramides and provitamin B5, the latter an additional humectant that helps improve skin barrier function. And, don’t let the fruity notes in the ingredients worry you if your skin is sensitive; it holds virtually zero fragrance.

Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, Pineapple ceramide, Provitamin B5 | Size: 1.69 ounces |  Pairs well with: Drunk Elephant Lala Retro Whipped Cream ($64)

The Ordinary Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5 Serum is a popular, lightweight serum designed to hydrate and replenish the skin. With a 2% concentration, this serum provides a balanced level of hydration without overwhelming the skin, fitting the bill as one of the best hyaluronic acid serums we tested. Its gentle formula makes it suitable for all skin types.

The addition of Vitamin B5 (panthenol) enhances the skin’s barrier function, promoting healing and reducing irritation. This combination of ingredients makes it a great option for people looking to address dryness, and dehydration and improve overall skin texture, remaining on a budget all the while.

“I love The Ordinary for its straightforward and effective ingredient list,” Holly J Coley, commerce deputy editor, shared. “My skin is incredibly dry — like, so dry that I use a facial oil and moisturizer or a regular basis. I found that this hyaluronic acid made it so that I didn’t have to put layer after layer of other products on, which was huge.”

She applied it to a damp face (typically after her shower) and was happy to notice it absorbed in about a minute. “It left my skin dewy, soft, and with a noticeable bounce,” she added.

One of the key benefits of this serum is its ability to provide immediate hydration, leaving the skin feeling smooth and soft. It works by replenishing moisture in the skin’s outer layers, preventing water loss and improving elasticity. The lightweight, non-greasy texture absorbs quickly, making it easy to layer with other skincare products, such as moisturizers and sunscreens. Since it doesn’t leave a sticky or heavy residue, it’s ideal for both daytime and nighttime use.

Despite its simplicity, The Ordinary Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5 Serum stands out for its efficacy and affordability. The brand is known for offering high-quality, science-backed products at accessible price points, and this serum is no exception. Better yet, it doesn’t contain any unnecessary fillers or fragrances, making it a great option for those with sensitive skin or anyone looking for a no-frills approach to skincare.

Size: 1 ounce | Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, Glycerin | Pairs well with: The Ordinary Natural Moisturizing Factors + HA ($14)

The Naturium Quadruple Hyaluronic Acid Serum 5% doesn’t only hydrate but provides multi-level moisture. In its formulation, it blends four different forms of hyaluronic acid, each one targeting different layers of the skin for maximum effectiveness.

The higher 5% concentration delivers a more potent dose of hydration than the rest of the industry’s litter, making it a powerful option for addressing dryness and dehydration.

“I’ve been using the Naturium Quadruple Hyaluronic Acid Serum 5% for a bit now, and I’m actually impressed with the results,” Kendall Cornish, former commerce writer/editor, shared. “The gel-like texture absorbs quickly into my (seriously dehydrated) skin, leaving it feeling plump, but without any sticky residue.”

If Naturium’s hyaluronic acid serum wasn’t enough of an overachiever, it also includes vitamin B5 (panthenol), which helps to soothe and support the skin’s natural barrier. This makes the serum suitable for a wide range of skin types, including sensitive and irritated skin.

To top if off, this serum holds a lightweight, non-greasy texture that absorbs quickly into the skin, leaving a refreshed, soft feel without any residue; this makes it seamless to layer with other skincare products in your regimen.

The hyaluronic acid serum is also formulated without parabens, sulfates or artificial fragrances, making it a clean and gentle option for those who are mindful of ingredient transparency. Its packaging features a sleek, air-tight pump bottle that helps preserve the potency of the active ingredients while making it easy to dispense the right amount of product.

Size: 1 ounce | Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, Vitamin B5, Glycerin | Pairs well with: Naturium Dew-Glow Moisturizer SPF 50 ($22)

The Neutrogena Hydro Boost Hyaluronic Acid Serum is an excellent choice for oily skin due to its lightweight, non-comedogenic formula, which hydrates without clogging pores. Oily skin can sometimes become dehydrated, leading to an overproduction of oil as the skin compensates for the lack of moisture. With a well-designed formulation that keeps hyaluronic acid as the mainstay ingredient, it ensures the skin stays hydrated throughout the day without feeling greasy or heavy. It also balances oil production, preventing the skin from becoming excessively oily or dry.

Neutrogena Hydro Boost Serum has a gel-like consistency that absorbs quickly into the skin, providing a smooth, refreshed feel without leaving a residue. This makes it ideal for daily use, even under makeup, as it creates a hydrated yet matte surface.

“The Neutrogena Hydro Boost Hyaluronic Acid Serum has been a really lovely addition to my (admittedly somewhat sparse) skincare routine,” Angela Tricarico, commerce streaming reporter, shared. “I started using it in tandem with the Hydro Boost Hyaluronic Acid Water Gel Cream and have seen a notable difference in my skin, which tends to be drier in the winter months.”

What’s more, the parts of Tricarico’s skin that are normally the driest are nice and soft, and her t-zone has been less oily since she started using this serum daily.

Neutrogena’s hyaluronic acid serum is designed to deliver long-lasting moisture, ensuring that the skin remains balanced and comfortable without triggering breakouts or excessive shine. It supports skin barrier function without exacerbating oiliness, and you’ll also appreciate how it’s enriched with glycerin, which helps retain water within the skin, while also offering antioxidant properties to protect the skin from environmental stressors. This makes the serum effective for maintaining skin health and preventing irritation or inflammation that can often occur in oily, and even acne-prone, skin.

Size: 1 ounce | Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, Vitamin B5, Glycerin | Pairs well with: Neutrogena Hydro Boost Hyaluronic Acid Gel Cream ($23)

The Three Ships Dew Drops Mushroom + Kakadu Plum + Hyaluronic Acid Serum is a lovely choice for sensitive skin due to its carefully selected, soothing ingredients designed to calm and hydrate without causing irritation. It’s distinctive for its inclusion of Tremella extract — a hyaluronic acid alternative — that has the potential to penetrate the epidermis (the outer layer of the skin, that is) deeper because of its smaller particle size compared to traditional hyaluronic acid.

Mushroom extract, one of the key ingredients, marries with Tremella extract to deliver powerful anti-inflammatory properties to reduce redness, irritation, and inflammation, which are common concerns for sensitive skin types. This makes the serum ideal for individuals who experience reactive skin or conditions like rosacea or eczema, as it helps restore balance without exacerbating sensitivity.

In addition to mushroom extract, the serum also contains Kakadu plum, which is rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. As we know, vitamin C is a superstar for its brightening effects and, in this formula, Kakadu plum helps to protect the skin from environmental stressors while promoting a more even complexion

“I’m majorly impressed by the results and quality of this serum and its all-natural ingredients,” Meaghan Seward, senior strategist of commerce audience optimization and discovery, shared. “I started testing this product just when my skin needed it most; I was just getting over a bad cold, and the cold of the winter was really starting to set in in December. My skin absorbed all the hydration it so desperately needed, leaving it clear, plump and rejuvenated.”

The best part, per Seward, is how well this serum layers with other products in her routine. “At first, I noticed a slight smell from the mushroom extract, but given that it’s natural rather than artificial fragrance, this really didn’t bother my sensitive skin,” she shared. “After all, these ingredients allow for the product to be 100% vegan, cruelty-free, gluten-free and pregnancy safe. It’s worth noting that it also contains vitamin C to help brighten skin tone, but should always be supported with SPF to protect your skin.”

The lightweight, non-greasy texture of this serum ensures it absorbs quickly without leaving a heavy residue, making it ideal for sensitive skin that is prone to feeling overwhelmed by thicker formulations. Together, these ingredients work synergistically to hydrate, protect and calm, making it a great addition to a sensitive skincare routine.

Size: 1 ounce | Key ingredients: Tremella extract (hyaluronic acid alternative), Kakadu plum, Red algae extract | Pairs well with: Three Ships Restore Ceramides + Gotu Kola Barrier Repair Cream ($37)

The Good Molecules Hyaluronic Acid Serum serves those with acne-prone skin due to its lightweight, noncomedogenic formula that delivers effective hydration without clogging pores. As imagined, one of the key challenges for individuals with acne is maintaining proper hydration while avoiding products that may contribute to breakouts or excess oil production. Unlike heavier creams or oils that can exacerbate acne by trapping bacteria or oil in the pores, the serum absorbs quickly and leaves the skin feeling refreshed and plump without any greasy residue. No congested skin here.

“If you’re looking for a kicked-up hyaluronic acid formula, Good Molecules is a great choice,” Miska Salemann, commerce reporter, shared. “It incorporates two forms of hyaluronic acid with different molecular weights, allowing it to penetrate the skin further for a deeper, total hydration. My favorite part about this formula is that it doesn’t require long-term use to start noticing results; your skin starts looking and feeling more hydrated right away.”

Given that this is a stronger formula, Salemann was slightly nervous there would be some stinging when she applied it, but she didn’t notice anything of the sort. “It went on quite gently and my skin seems softer, brighter, more subtle and plumped in the right places,” she added. “With time, I’d expect it would help smooth out some fine lines, too.”

Besides its ability to hydrate, the serum also helps to balance the skin’s moisture levels, which is crucial for acne management. Often, acne treatments like salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide can dry out the skin, leading to an imbalance where the skin compensates by producing even more oil. This can create a cycle that worsens acne. As a helpful agent, the Good Molecules Hyaluronic Acid Serum can break this cycle by replenishing moisture without triggering an overproduction of oil because of its inclusion of hyaluronic acid and lightweight properties.

The Good Molecules serum boasts a formula that’s void of harsh additives like parabens, sulfates or artificial fragrances, which can irritate sensitive, acne-prone skin. It also features a non-greasy formula that plumps at the same time which may mitigate the appearance of subtle acne scars due to its water-drenched aftereffect. ;

Size: 1 ounce | Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, Glycerin | Pairs well with: Good Molecules Lightweight Daily Moisturizer ($12)

After reviewing the lion’s share of La Roche-Posay, I can attest that its Hyalu B5 Pure Hyaluronic Acid Serum is a sent-from-above blessing for skin that needs some TLC. Hyaluronic acid aside, this serum contains vitamin B5 (panthenol), which has healing and anti-inflammatory properties that help to strengthen the skin’s barrier, reduce irritation and accelerate the skin’s natural repair process. In short, it’s a dreamboat for redness.

My skin is mostly dry and sensitive. I’m sometimes prone to redness near the apples of my cheeks. To prevent them from *actually* turning Snow White-apple red, I turn to La Roche-Posay’s nurturing formula that holds a one-of-a-kind cooling effect. The synergistic duo of hyaluronic acid and vitamin B5 works to restore moisture, soothe and calm redness caused by environmental stressors or underlying skin conditions like rosacea or eczema.

Big picture thinking now: La Roche-Posay’s commitment to using minimalist approach with dermatologically tested ingredients is crucial for those with sensitive or redness-prone skin. “I have acne-prone combination skin and Cerave is one of the few brands that has had my back over the years,” Salemann said. “The Hydrating Hyaluronic Acid Serum is super gentle and works wonders. Even a small amount goes a long way for hydration.”

With her skin being dry in the winter, applying this serum helps bring it back to life. “My face feels baby soft (like just-had-a-facial-soft), for the whole day,” she added. “I wouldn’t recommend it for someone living in a more humid or dewy climate, but for an East Coast winter — it’s an absolute everyday essential.”

This serum is formulated with three essential ceramides, which help to reinforce the skin’s natural barrier, ensuring that moisture stays locked in for longer periods; this helps to reduce moisture loss and prevent external irritants from penetrating the skin. It’s noncomedogenic, fragrance-free and dermatologist-tested, making it a soothing refresher before bedtime, though you can also use it in the morning.

The serum is also non-greasy and lightweight, allowing it to layer easily under other treatments without feeling heavy or sticky. Whether you’re looking for a boost of hydration or seeking to improve the overall appearance and texture of your skin, it’s a great option for balancing hydration levels.

Size: 1 ounce | Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, Ceramides, Glycerin | Pairs well with: CeraVe Daily Moisturizing Lotion with Hyaluronic Acid & Ceramides ($19)

While I’m beyond obsessed with the COSRX Snail Mucin 96% Power Repairing Essence ($20), it can’t steal all of the spotlight. That’s where the brand’s equally as good Hyaluronic Acid Intensive Cream comes in. It’s a rich, deeply hydrating moisturizer formulated with a high concentration of hyaluronic acid, attracting moisture to keep skin plump, smooth and hydrated.

I find that it’s perfect for my dehydrated skin, with the cream’s thick, luscious texture absorbing quickly without feeling heavy or greasy. After reviewing all of Charlotte Tilbury, its Magic Cream is one to rave about. First off, this hyaluronic acid cream is supremely luxurious with a melt-in-your-fingers consistency that leads to a soothing, smooth glow. It’s infused with ingredients like hyaluronic acid, aloe vera and peptides to deliver moisture deep into the skin, helping to reduce dryness each time I use it.

What sets Magic Cream apart from other moisturizers is its multitasking ability. Not only does it hydrate, but it also provides a radiant glow. On a scientific level, the formula contains light-reflecting particles that help create a soft, dewy finish, making it perfect for those who want a luminous complexion without the need for additional highlighters or makeup. “SkinCeuticals is revered by anyone who knows a thing about medical-grade skincare,” Coley said. “I’ve used HA products before but nothing as high-end. She said you can sense skin sensitivity a little bit when using this, so hydration layered on top (like one of the best night creams we reviewed) is key, as well as a daily SPF. “I would caution using this alongside any other highly active serums; it may make your face feel hot and overwhelm the skin,” she noted.

For its thoughtfully curated ingredient list, it’s a product suitable for those with dry or dehydrated skin, which can often exacerbate the appearance of hyperpigmentation. Not only that, this hyaluronic acid-infused primer is also clean, vegan and cruelty-free, making it a top-tier sustainable buy. Its green-tinted gel blends transparently into the skin as well, giving it a universally flattering look on all skin tones.
