“As someone who firmly believes good skincare — especially the basics — shouldn’t break the bank, I was really excited to try The Inkey List’s much-hyped hyaluronic acid serum — and I wasn’t disappointed!” Elana Fishman, Page Six Style and shopping director, said. “My skin’s always dry, but it gets particularly parched during the winter and this added a nice boost of hydration when layered beneath my usual moisturizer.”

It didn’t feel sticky on her skin, either (a common complaint with hyaluronic acid serums) and seemed to absorb nicely, leaving her complexion looking and feeling plump and nourished. “I haven’t noticed any breakouts or irritation after about a month of testing it, either, and my skin’s fairly sensitive,” Fishman added. “Do be careful when dispensing it; you only need a few drops to get the job done, and the packaging makes it easy to pour out too much at once. But again, at $10 a bottle, it’s not the end of the world if you go through it quickly!”

Additionally, the INKEY List Hyaluronic Acid Serum works synergistically with other skincare products to improve overall skin texture. When used as part of a consistent skincare routine, it enhances the effectiveness of exfoliating acids or treatments that target uneven skin tone or surface texture. The serum’s ability to keep skin hydrated creates an optimal environment for these active ingredients to work more effectively, leading to smoother, more refined skin over time.

To add the cherry on top of the skincare sundae, this serum contains a multi-molecular form of hyaluronic acid which penetrates deeply into the skin’s surface to provide additional nourishment. Consider this your skincare masterclass. Below, find the 411 on hyaluronic acid: what it is, how to use it and best practices for integrating the ingredient into your skincare routine.

“Hyaluronic acid (H.A.) is a polysaccharide (sugar string) substance found naturally in human skin, eyes, and joints, which acts as a natural lubricant, volume support and moisturizer,” Jessica Krant, MD, MPH, a board-certified dermatologist at NYC’s Laser & Skin Surgery Center told the New York Post. “It’s the material that surrounds and supports collagen in our skin.”

What’s more, it’s a staple ingredient for hydration due to its properties. “The key benefit of hyaluronic acid is its ability to bind water,” Adarsh Vijay Mudgil, MD, a dual board-certified dermatologist and founder of NYC’s Mudgil Dermatology PC, told The Post. “It can bind 1,000 times its weight in water, making it an ideal moisturizer.”

As mentioned above, there are plenty of hyaluronic acid benefits, as the ingredient, when incorporated, makes for an incredible moisturizer and serum for rejuvenated skin. “In topical products, it also helps make the skin surface more ‘translucent’ to other products, helping them penetrate more effectively through the skin surface barrier,” Dr. Krant adds.

It can also act as a humectant, drawing moisture from the air and holding it against the skin.

Ahead, our dermatologist experts share the 411 on how to use hyaluronic acid.

According to Dr. Mudgil, a topical preparation can be used daily to multiple times per day depending on one’s skin type.” Those with dry skin can use H.A. products more frequently without issue, too.”

Because it’s a natural substance, it’s also well-tolerated by just about everyone. “There’s really no skin type that can’t use it,” Dr. Nazarian noted. “Even super sensitive skin can use this ingredient safely and can use it daily, even several times a day. It can be used around the eyes and shows improvement within minutes —  super quickly. Ideally, it’s used with an emollient or something to seal the skin barrier to enhance its effects; humectant plus emollient is the perfect combo.”

Nazarian loves it best for dry skin and acne-prone skin, especially when paired with an emollient. “People with early signs of aging, like fine lines, can also benefit from using hyaluronic acid because it can minimize those lines very nicely, even within a few hours,” she highlighted. “Additionally, I like suggesting hyaluronic acid for people that are on a skincare regimen that may be somewhat irritating (such as acne regimens).”

“It’s absolutely okay to combine hyaluronic acid with retinol, vitamin C or niacinamide; it’s a perfect complement to these ingredients,” Nazarian said. “It does not work to treat acne as a monotherapy, and I would never recommend it as such. On the flip side, it doesn’t clog pores or cause acne, so it’s perfectly safe to use for acne-prone skin.”

The percentage of hyaluronic acid to use largely depends on your skin type and tolerability. For instance, if you have more sensitive skin, you’ll want to use a lower percentage, like 0.5%. However, if you’re not a newbie to hyaluronic acid or find your skin to be a veteran of many serums, you can use between 1% to 2%.

When researching hyaluronic acid skincare products before testing, we noticed that some brands highlighted if a formulation was a low-molecular-weight, high-molecular-weight or multi-molecular.

“Hyaluronic acid is found naturally in our tissue, mostly in a high molecular weight form, although it does get broken down and is found as a low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid as well,” Nazarian explained. “The different weights may signal different cellular responses in the skin, triggering different pathways of healing and repair mechanisms, but they also have varying levels of penetration into the skin, meaning, you find different types in different areas and levels of the skin and body.”

So, the thought is that perhaps using a combination of molecular weights will trigger different complementary pathways and will lead to even better results than just high molecular weight alone. Generally, a low-molecular weight can penetrate deeper into the skin, but may also be more irritating. Higher-molecular weight stays on the surface for hydration.

“Plus, we know that the larger the size, the harder it is to penetrate into the skin, and we also know that too small may actually have harmful effects on the tissue. So it’s alllll about balance,” she commented.

Somewhat surprisingly, companies are not really stating what level of molecular weight they’re using in their products. But, Nazarian (and The Post Shopping team) thinks this is a trend that we should be looking for in the future.

Based on our testing, the most effective hyaluronic acid serum is the Drunk Elephant B-Hydra Intensive Hydration Serum for its ability to douse the skin in hydration and alleviate dry, flaky skin.

We also recommend The Ordinary Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5 Serum if you’re on a budget, and the SkinCeuticals Hyaluronic Acid Intensifier Multi-Glycan if you’re willing to splurge a bit more.

You’ve seen it before — the skincare commercial where someone joyfully splashes water on their face, usually right before the screen flashes the words “hyaluronic acid” in bold.

That signature water imagery? It’s not just for show. It perfectly captures what the best hyaluronic acid serums are designed to do: hydrate, plump and refresh your skin like a tall glass of water for your face.

So, what is hyaluronic acid, really? Despite the slightly intimidating name, it’s not a harsh chemical. In fact, it’s a naturally occurring substance found in your skin, joints and eyes. As a powerful humectant, hyaluronic acid draws moisture from the environment and locks it into your skin — making it an essential ingredient in many moisturizers, serums and even lip balms. The result? Smooth, supple skin that looks healthier and more hydrated.

Whether you’re wondering how to use hyaluronic acid, whether hyaluronic acid causes acne, or how it compares to niacinamide, there’s no denying the ingredient’s versatility. It’s loved by dermatologists and skincare lovers alike, and the benefits of hyaluronic acid go far beyond hydration (think: improved skin texture, minimized fine lines and even soothing support for sensitive or acne-prone skin).

To help you navigate the best options on the market, we’ve rounded up top-rated products — from the best overall hyaluronic acid serum to a gentle lip balm, nighttime serum and more. No matter your skin type or concern, there’s a hyaluronic acid solution for you.

“Hyaluronic acid is a natural substance found in our skin that helps keep it moisturized and plump,” Rachel Nazarian, MD, board-certified dermatologist at Schweiger Dermatology Group in NYC, told the New York Post. “Because of its ability to draw and hold water, it’s referred to as a ‘humectant moisturizer’ — and keeps skin moisturized throughout the day, [minimizing] the appearance of fine lines and superficial wrinkles.”

Ahead, find the alluring, barrier-repairing serums, face masks, lip balms, and lotions that’ll bring your skin back to life (when used consistently, that is). Once you begin dousing your face and body with HA, you’ll be in for a dewy, glowing-from-within treat.

The Drunk Elephant B-Hydra Intensive Hydration Serum is an incredibly moisturizing, humectant-forward serum that wears many hats in its formulation. For one, it helps minimize the look of fine lines, helps reverse and alleviate the impact of my dry, flaky skin and essentially floods my skin with nourishment. It’s the crème de la crème of hyaluronic acid serums, namely for its ability to mask away dullness and conquer even the driest of regions on the face.

Leave it to me — I’ve reviewed all of Drunk Elephant and the brand goes beyond its photo-worthy matte white lotions and potions with a fun, neon cap. The magic is what lies inside and, in this case, it’s hydration.

Drunk Elephant’s B-Hydra Intensive Hydration Serum is packed with pineapple ceramides and provitamin B5, the latter an additional humectant that helps improve skin barrier function. And, don’t let the fruity notes in the ingredients worry you if your skin is sensitive; it holds virtually zero fragrance.

Key ingredients: Hyaluronic acid, Pineapple ceramide, Provitamin B5 | Size: 1.69 ounces |  Pairs well with: Drunk Elephant Lala Retro Whipped Cream ($64)

The Ordinary Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5 Serum is a popular, lightweight serum designed to hydrate and replenish the skin. With a 2% concentration, this serum provides a balanced level of hydration without overwhelming the skin, fitting the bill as one of the best hyaluronic acid serums we tested. Its gentle formula makes it suitable for all skin types.

The addition of Vitamin B5 (panthenol) enhances the skin’s barrier function, promoting healing and reducing irritation. This combination of ingredients makes it a great option for people looking to address dryness, and dehydration and improve overall skin texture, remaining on a budget all the while.

“I love The Ordinary for its straightforward and effective ingredient list,” Holly J Coley, commerce deputy editor, shared. “My skin is incredibly dry — like, so dry that I use a facial oil and moisturizer or a regular basis. I found that this hyaluronic acid made it so that I didn’t have to put layer after layer of other products on, which was huge.”

She applied it to a damp face (typically after her shower) and was happy to notice it absorbed in about a minute. “It left my skin dewy, soft, and with a noticeable bounce,” she added.

Consider this your skincare masterclass. Below, find the 411 on hyaluronic acid: what it is, how to use it and best practices for integrating the ingredient into your skincare routine.

“Hyaluronic acid (H.A.) is a polysaccharide (sugar string) substance found naturally in human skin, eyes, and joints, which acts as a natural lubricant, volume support and moisturizer,” Jessica Krant, MD, MPH, a board-certified dermatologist at NYC’s Laser & Skin Surgery Center told the New York Post. “It’s the material that surrounds and supports collagen in our skin.”

What’s more, it’s a staple ingredient for hydration due to its properties. “The key benefit of hyaluronic acid is its ability to bind water,” Adarsh Vijay Mudgil, MD, a dual board-certified dermatologist and founder of NYC’s Mudgil Dermatology PC, told The Post. “It can bind 1,000 times its weight in water, making it an ideal moisturizer.”

As mentioned above, there are plenty of hyaluronic acid benefits, as the ingredient, when incorporated, makes for an incredible moisturizer and serum for rejuvenated skin. “In topical products, it also helps make the skin surface more ‘translucent’ to other products, helping them penetrate more effectively through the skin surface barrier,” Dr. Krant adds.

It can also act as a humectant, drawing moisture from the air and holding it against the skin.

Ahead, our dermatologist experts share the 411 on how to use hyaluronic acid.

According to Dr. Mudgil, a topical preparation can be used daily to multiple times per day depending on one’s skin type.” Those with dry skin can use H.A. products more frequently without issue, too.”

Because it’s a natural substance, it’s also well-tolerated by just about everyone. “There’s really no skin type that can’t use it,” Dr. Nazarian noted. “Even super sensitive skin can use this ingredient safely and can use it daily, even several times a day. It can be used around the eyes and shows improvement within minutes —  super quickly. Ideally, it’s used with an emollient or something to seal the skin barrier to enhance its effects; humectant plus emollient is the perfect combo.”

Nazarian loves it best for dry skin and acne-prone skin, especially when paired with an emollient. “People with early signs of aging, like fine lines, can also benefit from using hyaluronic acid because it can minimize those lines very nicely, even within a few hours,” she highlighted. “Additionally, I like suggesting hyaluronic acid for people that are on a skincare regimen that may be somewhat irritating (such as acne regimens).”

“It’s absolutely okay to combine hyaluronic acid with retinol, vitamin C or niacinamide; it’s a perfect complement to these ingredients,” Nazarian said. “It does not work to treat acne as a monotherapy, and I would never recommend it as such. On the flip side, it doesn’t clog pores or cause acne, so it’s perfectly safe to use for acne-prone skin.”

The percentage of hyaluronic acid to use largely depends on your skin type and tolerability. For instance, if you have more sensitive skin, you’ll want to use a lower percentage, like 0.5%. However, if you’re not a newbie to hyaluronic acid or find your skin to be a veteran of many serums, you can use between 1% to 2%.

When researching hyaluronic acid skincare products before testing, we noticed that some brands highlighted if a formulation was a low-molecular-weight, high-molecular-weight or multi-molecular.

“Hyaluronic acid is found naturally in our tissue, mostly in a high molecular weight form, although it does get broken down and is found as a low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid as well,” Nazarian explained. “The different weights may signal different cellular responses in the skin, triggering different pathways of healing and repair mechanisms, but they also have varying levels of penetration into the skin, meaning, you find different types in different areas and levels of the skin and body.”

So, the thought is that perhaps using a combination of molecular weights will trigger different complementary pathways and will lead to even better results than just high molecular weight alone. Generally, a low-molecular weight can penetrate deeper into the skin, but may also be more irritating. Higher-molecular weight stays on the surface for hydration.

“Plus, we know that the larger the size, the harder it is to penetrate into the skin, and we also know that too small may actually have harmful effects on the tissue. So it’s alllll about balance,” she commented.

Somewhat surprisingly, companies are not really stating what level of molecular weight they’re using in their products. But, Nazarian (and The Post Shopping team) thinks this is a trend that we should be looking for in the future.

Based on our testing, the most effective hyaluronic acid serum is the Drunk Elephant B-Hydra Intensive Hydration Serum for its ability to douse the skin in hydration and alleviate dry, flaky skin.

We also recommend The Ordinary Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5 Serum if you’re on a budget, and the SkinCeuticals Hyaluronic Acid Intensifier Multi-Glycan if you’re willing to splurge a bit more.

Nearly 45 years after starting her fashion brand in the garment district, Nicole Miller is still all-in on New York.

Four days a week, the designer treks from her Tribeca apartment to her Seventh Avenue office building — the same one where she built her fashion collection nearly 45 years ago.

Under Miller’s influence, New Yorkers began grabbing up the “boho chic” staples — hobo bags, wide-leg jeans, velvet slip dresses, and romantic, billowing blouses — that still influence American style today.

But before Miller built a brand worth nearly $700 million or dressed celebrities like Angelina Jolie and Beyoncé, she was like many high schoolers: making her clothes on a sewing machine at home in the Berkshires.

That led to studying at the Rhode Island School of Design, where classmates included future bohemian icons like David Byrne and Tina Weymouth of Talking Heads. After graduating in 1973, Miller beelined it to New York City.

“Where else would you go?” she asked — or score a one-bedroom Upper East Side apartment for $240 a month? (Fourth-floor walkups in the neighborhood now run about $3,500.)

Off-hours were spent at Studio 54, Max’s Kansas City, roller-skating at The Roxy, and attending Andy Warhol’s blind-date dinners at The Odeon, where everyone brought a blind date for someone else. Miller became part of that artistic downtown scene through her college friends, meeting the pop art king through photographer Paige Powell.

After early gigs as a design assistant, Miller joined the New York dress company P.J. Walsh, where she first met Bud Konheim, a brutally frank and fast-talking executive.

Though Miller was generally soft-spoken and relaxed, she found they made a good business pair, and in 1982, the duo quit their jobs to launch her namesake company. Konheim scraped together $100,000 from family and friends, and Miller pitched in $15,000 from her personal savings.

The risk was worth it: The brand struck gold in its first year with an easy-to-wear dress that flattered the body by draping easily across the waist, appearing almost belted at the hips. Her knack for making women feel relaxed but glamorous took off, and she racked up $5 million in sales in the first year.

Meanwhile, Miller was hitting the town with friends Jay McInerney, author of Bright Lights, Big City, and Balthazar restaurateur Keith McNally. As for how she met her longtime friend Candace Bushnell, author of Sex and the City?

“Well,” Miller said, “Candace used to date my husband.”

All in all, “It was just fun. Everybody was drinking too much,” she said. “There were always some new trendy restaurants in New York. We were at The Odeon all the time along with the whole art world.”

Being in such creative company fueled Miller’s own vision, and after her first hit dress became a magnet for cheap knockoffs, she imagined something new: designer ties for both men and women.

They took off in the late 1980s, when a security guard in Miller’s former Madison Avenue store wore a tie printed with ticket stubs to his night job at the Metropolitan Opera. A Met staffer noticed the flashy neckwear, and the historic music hub soon placed a hefty order for its gift shop.

Within two years, Miller’s novelty neckties became a $12 million business, with brands like Frito Lay and Veuve Clicquot wanting to collaborate. “In the beginning, nobody was territorial about their logos,” Miller said. “But with the candy tie” — a bestselling design featuring chocolate snacks hand-drawn by Miller and her team on silk — “we had M&M’s, Hershey’s, Nestlé, and Mars. They were like, ‘Thank you for making us a tie, but next time don’t put us with our competitors.’”

Miller’s booming tie business unexpectedly led to love. After a meeting with Absolut about their own custom cravats, one executive cajoled Miller into making her first-ever wedding gown for his friend, along with a series of bridesmaid dresses.

“I couldn’t say no because it was Absolut Vodka,” Miller said with a laugh. At the wedding, she met her husband, Kim Taipale, a former investment banker and lawyer. They married in 1996, with former Mayor Rudy Giuliani officiating at City Hall. “We had Champagne and caviar afterward,” she said. “He was such a good mayor, and now he’s gotten so weird.”

When wedding trends loosened up, the designer started offering some of her evening dresses in white. Then shoppers started asking for some of her cocktail dresses for bridesmaids, so she whipped up a bridesmaid dress line. “We kept getting asked to do these things. It happened spontaneously,” she said.

Meanwhile, the tie revenue allowed her to spend more on runway shows and cast major 1990s supermodels like Naomi Campbell, Christy Turlington, and Linda Evangelista, turning the media spotlight on the designer.

“They were very serious about their profession. And they were always really nice. It’s funny, because some of the second-tier models were always a little attitude-y,” she said. (Ever the professional, Miller declined to name names, but did share that Tyra Banks was “one of the nicest models ever.”)

The supermodels’ Midas effect led to some celebrity dressing and wardrobing for movies and TV. Cardi B, Angelina Jolie, Kim Kardashian, Brad Pitt, and Kim Cattrall have worn the label.

The designer got famous enough to make her own Barbie doll, along with a luxe collection for The Price Is Right contestants. She’s also served as a judge for the Miss USA and Miss Universe pageants.

But in 2022, three years after her partner Konheim’s death, Miller decided it was time to take back some of her time. She sold a majority stake in the business and set up licenses for furniture, kitchenware, and beauty products. You probably have a Nicole Miller umbrella somewhere in your apartment.

But Miller soon realized she couldn’t avoid the style spotlight entirely.

In 2024, she started selling a new collection on QVC. A few times each month, she and her son Palmer Taipale, who works as her brand’s senior e-commerce and marketplace associate, go live on-air to front the label.

Sometimes, they even beam into their livestream from Miller’s Seventh Avenue showroom.

Nicole Miller’s brand turns 45 next year, but the designer is getting a jump on the milestone.

Today, she unveils a signature collection for the first time in three years. Some styles riff on old favorites — there are taxi cab prints and a strapless bandage dress made with the designer’s novelty neckties.

The designer has even reimagined her famous “baseball dress,” a sporty white tank dress with red stitching worn by Geena Davis to the 1992 premiere of “A League of Their Own.” The new version is longer, with sequins.

And Miller continues to feed off the city’s energy. She and her husband live in a 3,100-square-foot apartment that used to be three separate spaces — including the original apartment where she used to roller-skate around her living room on weekends. Their son also lives in the building.

“There’s just so much to be inspired by here, just walking around all of the different neighborhoods. If you’re a theater buff, you can go to the theater, or go to concerts and all kinds of things,” she said, continuing to scout new haunts. (Current favorites include Wild Cherry at A24’s Cherry Lane Theatre and Patsy’s Pizzeria in Harlem.)

Miller’s hard, enterprising work has also earned her a Sag Harbor manse, where the designer likes to waterski in the summer. She only recently stopped wakeboarding. (“If you wipe out, you wipe out hard,” she explained.) Friends include Countess Luann de Lesseps and Dexter producer Sara Colleton.

As for the company she’s built, Miller said, “I just look at it as, I’m still having a good time, and I’m enjoying what I’m doing.”

Expensive s—t that’s worth it, French edition.

Bethenny Frankel loves a drugstore find, so when she raves about a pricey beauty product, you know it’s the real deal. And when the “RHONY” legend recently posted about my favorite luxury French skin care brand, it was a true IYKYK moment.

In the Instagram Reel, the “Just B” podcast host shares that she is “obsessed” with the Yon-Ka Paris Vitamin C Serum.

“It goes on like a dream,” she says, raving that it could be her “new favorite serum.”

Made with 99.9% natural-origin ingredients, the formula helps lighten dark spots, brighten tone and boost radiance. It’s in an oily base that sinks right in — but leaves skin moisturized and supple all day. (Plus, as Frankel says, a little goes a long way.)

The “Just B” host follows the serum with the brand’s “invisible” SPF 50 Mineral Fluid Sunscreen, saying, “It hydrates, it’s not sticky, and it doesn’t burn your eyes.”

I understand why the entrepreneur loves the vitamin C serum so — I’ve used it so often that mine is nearly empty. C’est triste!

It costs $178 for a full bottle, making it one of the more expensive products I own — yet, it also earns my “worth it” status. I apply it with chilled cryo sticks in the morning for an unparalleled glow (and sensorial experience) that has people complimenting my skin more than ever. It’s perfect with gua sha as well.

While it’s rich enough to use alone in summer, as the weather cools, I layer it with Hydra N°1 Crème for the softest skin all day. Even better, the line is free of perfumes and chemicals that irritate my sensitive skin.

Used at luxury French spas like Printemps in Paris and New York City, Yon-Ka recently launched at major beauty retailers like Nordstrom and Ulta — so it’s about to become a well-known skin care staple stateside, too.

The other half of the sun care program Frankel’s “obsessed” with.

A hydrating, alcohol-free mist, seen on “Emily in Paris.”

A lightweight moisturizer that keeps even dry skin hydrated and soft all day.

news.originalContent:

The fantasy is here to stay.

Page Six Style has exclusively learned that the $50 million Fantasy Bra Kylie Jenner wore during the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026 is set to return to the Jacob & Co. NYC boutique, where it will be made available for private purchase.

In the past, most Fantasy Bras have been returned to the jeweler, disassembled, and made into various pieces of jewelry to be sold. Others have been put on display for fans to admire.

However, a representative for the brand told us Jenner’s bejeweled brassiere will remain intact for one lucky buyer.

It’s unclear if the price tag will remain at $50 million, but the bra could be invaluable to a certain buyer: Jenner herself.

Perhaps the multimillionaire makeup mogul might snap up the sparkly piece to commemorate her big catwalk moment; it’d also make a truly epic Christmas present from  boyfriend Timothée Chalamet or mom Kris Jenner, both of whom were cheering her on in the audience.

After all, the nearly four-pound piece was specifically made to fit Jenner’s “445 cc, moderate profile, half under the muscle, silicone” chest.

Whomever winds up spending the big bucks on the glittering lingerie will own a piece of history; this year’s VS show featured the event’s most expensive Fantasy Bra by far.

The previous record-holder was Gisele Bündchen’s Red Hot Fantasy Bra, which debuted in 2000 and was valued $15 million at the time — comparative chump change!

Jenner’s Jacob & Co. creation featured a 75.54-carat Fancy Vivid yellow diamond at its center, which alone is worth $22 million.

Another 4,409 diamonds totaling 1,373 carats make up the rest of the jewel-encrusted bra, each hand-set in a custom 18-karat gold mount.

news.originalContent:
US president has continued to support data centres in advance of midterms, despite growing opposition from Republicans.

United States President Donald Trump has said AI data centres should pay “dividends” to communities, in a shift before the midterm elections.

“If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a ‘dividend'” Trump said in a post on Truth Social on Wednesday.

The president’s comments come after he doubled down on his support for data centres, a stance seen as one of several political liabilities for Republicans in the run-up to the midterm election, as Trump’s approval rating has hit record lows.

Polls show dismal support for such centres amid concerns about the sprawling complexes’ water and energy use.

In the post, Trump advised companies that they could make the centres popular if they “pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a ‘dividend’.”

“I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck,” he said. “MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!!”

Several top Republican candidates have opposed data centres before the midterm polls, with the issue emerging as an area of rare bipartisan consensus in advance of the November 3 vote.

Republican Senate candidates, including Ken Paxton in Texas, Mike Rogers in Michigan and John Husted in Ohio, have all called for more restrictions and oversight on the centres, in a reversal of earlier positions.

The issue featured prominently in a recent debate in Iowa, where Republican Senate Candidate Ashley Hinson said the local level should decide whether to build AI data centres.

Despite the shifting sentiment, Trump in late August issued an impassioned defence of data centres, decrying what he called “the anti-Data Center movement” as a gift to China.

“The only reason that communities throughout the USA should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” Trump wrote at the time.

“If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign.”

Trump has taken several measures to accelerate data centre development, including issuing an executive order last year that called for measures to fast-track permitting and environmental review. The order promised to use federal land for the “expeditious and orderly development of data centers”.

Trump has also backed a voluntary pledge by AI companies to cover the full cost of the electricity data centres use, but has avoided supporting legally binding federal restrictions.

A Gallup poll conducted in March suggested that 71 percent of Americans opposed establishing AI data centres in their areas.

An ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll released on Wednesday identified a similar rate of disapproval, with 72 percent of respondents saying that they opposed building new data centres in their communities.

news.originalContent:
Russia will send on Thursday its first diesel tanker to the US to an undisclosed port.

Russia will send its first tanker of diesel fuel to the United States on Thursday, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters amid a deal with US President Donald Trump.

The vessel will have 40,000 tonnes of fuel, but Novak, who made his remarks on Wednesday, did not name which US port the fuel would be delivered to.

Russia lifted its ban on diesel exports on October 9, which Moscow originally put in place to tackle the country’s shortages as Ukrainian-led drone strikes hindered production capacity.

The shipment comes despite setbacks for Russia’s diesel output. Earlier this month, Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence said that drone strikes knocked out at least half of Russia’s oil refining capacity, forcing cuts at Russia’s top diesel-producing refineries.

“Additional shipments will follow, of course. There were agreements reached between the two leaders. We will meet the United States’ needs, to the extent of our capabilities,” the RIA Novosti news agency quoted Novak as saying.

That was echoed by US special envoy Steve Witkoff, who has been meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin for talks in St Petersburg.

“We are preparing deliveries of several vessels, the tankers, right now. They will go one after another. The financial component should be provided,” he said, adding that Russia would also be able to supply fertilisers in “large quantities” to the US market.

US President Donald Trump had previously said that Moscow would export 300,000 tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.

US consumers have continued to face high prices at the petrol station, particularly for diesel fuel, a pressing point as the country heads into midterm elections in less than two weeks. The average price for a gallon of diesel is $6.31 ($1.70 per litre), according to the American Automobile Association (AAA). While prices remain well over the $6 mark, they are on the downturn. The average price a month ago was $6.51.

news.originalContent:
The pledge, which Trump says will go through accounts with his name, comes two weeks before the US midterms.

Elon Musk has pledged to give one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next year – a gift that could be worth more than $10bn.

“This will be the first of many,” the world’s richest man wrote on X on Monday.

About 73 million children under 18 live in the US, according to US Census Bureau data.

At Friday’s closing price of $146.03, the pledge would be worth about $10.7bn.

President Donald Trump thanked Musk on his Truth Social platform, and claimed the shares would be given to children “through TRUMP ACCOUNTS”, the tax-friendly investment accounts for children created under his signature tax and spending law last year.

The pledge comes two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.

Musk is the biggest known donor in the run-up to those elections, having given more than $276m to Republican groups since July.

Musk has not said which children will qualify, when the shares will be handed over, or how.

So how might the giveaway work, and who stands to gain?

Here’s what you need to know:

SpaceX, the world’s seventh-largest company, began trading on the Nasdaq in June at an initial public offering price of $135 per share.
That price has been volatile. SpaceX shares have fallen 35.3 percent since peaking days after the listing.

The shares are currently trading at around $146 a share. Every $1 move in the share price will change the gift’s value by about $73m.

Musk owns 4.8 billion shares in SpaceX outright, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in August.

Including unvested awards and stock options, his stake rises to about 6.4 billion shares, or 48.4 percent of the company.

Giving away 73 million shares would reduce his outright holding by about 1.5 percent, barely affecting his control of the company. That’s because his voting power, which is currently about 82 percent because SpaceX has two classes of shares, would fall by only 0.1 percentage points, according to a Bloomberg Opinion calculation.

It would be the largest single gift linked to Trump accounts so far.

Trump said the shares would be held in Trump accounts, and Musk thanked Brad Gerstner, the tech investor behind the accounts, for “helping enable this”.

Nearly 70 million Trump accounts have been opened, one for every child under 18 with a Social Security number, according to the White House. Investments held in Trump accounts can roll up with tax deferred until they are withdrawn when a child turns 18. Alternatively, they can be rolled into a tax-friendly IRA – a retirement account for adults – and continue with the tax-friendly status.

Under Treasury rules published on September 30, donors can now gift individual company stock to children via the accounts. Families and friends making regular contributions to a child’s Trump account are limited to investing low-risk index funds.

Families cannot refuse the shares on behalf of their children and generally cannot sell them for five years, or until the end of the year the child turns 17 if that comes sooner.

Musk cannot sell or trade most of his SpaceX shares until June 2027, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The accounts carry the president’s name, and Trump has tied himself closely to the gift.

He thanked Musk on Truth Social, saying the pledge was “exactly what was envisioned when we created TRUMP ACCOUNTS”.

The White House has presented the accounts as a signature achievement of Trump’s tax law, noting that “every single Democrat voted against” the legislation.

The pledge also marks a public reconciliation. Musk and Trump fell out in 2025 over Trump’s tax-and-spending bill, a rift Trump later called a “little dispute”.

Children will be gaining a share for free, but the gift could also save Musk money.

Donors who give appreciated stock to charity avoid capital gains tax and can usually claim a deduction, the US broadcaster CNBC reported.

As SpaceX’s founder, Musk paid very little for his shares, and selling $10.7bn of them could mean a tax bill of up to about $2.5bn.

It is “a popular practice for particularly high-income taxpayers that would otherwise be paying a high rate”, Will McBride, chief economist at the Tax Foundation, told the broadcaster in May.

Ann Lipton, a law professor at the University of Colorado Boulder, told Inc. magazine that millions of shareholders unable to sell would also have an interest in SpaceX’s success and in “minimising its regulatory burdens”.

For Mitchell Downey, an economist at Stockholm University’s Institute for International Economic Studies who studies political influence in the US, the more striking part of the pledge is what he called “the horseshoe aspect of this” – the idea that right-wing and left-wing policies can curve around and meet.

For decades, progressives have backed the concept of Child Development Accounts, investment accounts for every newborn designed to reduce inequality in wealth, he said. The idea was associated with groups such as the Democracy Collaborative but struggled to gain federal support. Now the idea may become more mainstream as a result of Musk’s gift and Trump accounts.

“It always felt like it might be out of reach,” Downey said. “But I don’t see how Musk’s proposal would be possible without building some infrastructure like this.”

The pledge comes just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the two houses of Congress. All seats in the House of Representatives and one-third of the Senate are up for re-election.

Trump’s approval rating has meanwhile fallen to a record low of 33 percent, according to a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll, with many political observers expecting to see the Republicans lose seats to the Democratic Party as a result.

Musk, who campaigned with Trump in 2024 and spearheaded the president’s Department of Government Efficiency initiative to reduce the size of the federal workforce, has contributed heavily to Republican candidates in advance of the midterm elections.

Downey said he does not believe the pledge raises legal concerns.

“Individuals are allowed to spend their money in support of a politician,” he told Al Jazeera. “The law only gets violated when either it isn’t publicly reported, or it is part of an explicit and documented quid-pro-quo.”

But he said it does raise ethical concerns, though not ones unique to Musk’s approach.

Those concerns relate to “the outsized role that external donors play in US elections”, Downey said. In his view, they apply much like when someone spends heavily on television advertisements for a candidate.

Downey said the precedent was “hard to assess”.

Because Musk is the richest person in modern history, he said, it is perhaps unsurprising that he is “doing something that involves more money than other very rich people have done”.

He pointed to the Gates Foundation’s spending over the past three decades as “a different type of ‘gift to the public’”. The difference, he said, is that the Gates Foundation focuses funding on health crises in countries in Africa and South Asia – not on voters in the US.

Last year, Gates pledged to “give away virtually all my wealth through the Gates Foundation over the next 20 years to the cause of saving and improving lives around the world”.

news.originalContent:
Hubbard was jailed after Russia said he fought alongside Ukrainian forces against Russia.

American Stephen Hubbard has been freed from a Russian prison and is on his way home after United States President Donald Trump said his administration had secured his release.

“Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family,” Trump wrote in a social media post on Wednesday, adding that the US was not required to give anything in return for the release of the 74-year-old former teacher from Michigan.

The deal came during a visit to Russia by a top US envoy, and just days after Trump took a series of actions seen as beneficial to Moscow.

Hubbard, whose family says had been living in Ukraine since before Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, was tried and convicted in a closed-door trial, with Russian prosecutors saying he had signed a contract with the Ukrainian military and had fought alongside its forces before being captured. He was sentenced to seven years in prison in 2024.

The US had declared Hubbard a wrongfully detained American.

Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff, who is in Russia for talks with President Vladimir Putin on the Ukraine war, told him that “our whole nation sends their thanks” and that Putin was a “humanitarian” for allowing Hubbard to walk free. Witkoff briefly met with Hubbard in St. Petersburg after his release, telling him, “from today is a new life for you”.

The release came at a dynamic moment in relations between the US, Ukraine and Russia, with the Washington-Kyiv relationship under strain at the same time that the Trump administration has pursued policies which Ukraine says have rewarded Putin.

Those include Trump’s decision last week to waive sanctions on Russia imposed by a bill that the US Congress overwhelmingly passed to support Ukraine.

Named after the late South Carolina Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, the legislation targeted the flow of financial resources fuelling Moscow’s war on Ukraine.

That reversal followed Trump’s announcement of a deal to import Russian diesel fuel in an effort to curb high gas prices before next month’s US midterm elections.

Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff, who is in Russia for talks with President Vladimir Putin on the Ukraine war, told him that “our whole nation sends their thanks” and that Putin was a “humanitarian” for allowing Hubbard to walk free. Witkoff briefly met with Hubbard in St. Petersburg after his release, telling him, “from today is a new life for you”.

The release came at a dynamic moment in relations between the US, Ukraine and Russia, with the Washington-Kyiv relationship under strain at the same time that the Trump administration has pursued policies which Ukraine says have rewarded Putin.

Those include Trump’s decision last week to waive sanctions on Russia imposed by a bill that the US Congress overwhelmingly passed to support Ukraine.

Named after the late South Carolina Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, the legislation targeted the flow of financial resources fuelling Moscow’s war on Ukraine.

That reversal followed Trump’s announcement of a deal to import Russian diesel fuel in an effort to curb high gas prices before next month’s US midterm elections.

news.originalContent:
Lander says dozens remain in Israeli custody after being detained while helping Palestinian farmers harvest olives.

United States Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander says he has been released from Israeli military custody with a warning after being detained alongside dozens of volunteers helping Palestinian farmers harvest olives in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday.

But several dozen others, including rabbis and international volunteers, remain in detention, according to Lander, who called them to be released immediately.

“I’ve been released from IDF custody with a ‘warning,’ apparently because of my public profile,” Lander wrote on X. “I told them I wasn’t even a congressmember yet, just a nominee.”

Lander, a former New York City comptroller and mayoral candidate, was among approximately 80 volunteers detained by Israeli soldiers and police near the village of Nahalin, outside Bethlehem, according to the Israeli organisation Rabbis for Human Rights.

The group, which included American, Israeli, Palestinian, British and Canadian volunteers, had been accompanying Palestinian farmers for about two hours when Israeli forces arrived and informed them that they were in a closed military zone.

The volunteers were then taken to a police station, according to Rabbis for Human Rights.

The Israeli government has not responded to a request for comment.

news.originalContent:
Experts say conflicts and uncertainty are accelerating efforts to strengthen regional military capacity.

Qatar, Turkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia signed a deal on Wednesday to deepen their defence industry cooperation, reflecting a broader effort by countries in the region to widen their network of security partners amid the prolonged US-Israel war with Iran.

The four countries signed the memorandum of understanding in Doha, building on existing military projects through joint production, technology transfers and more closely integrated supply chains.

The initiative comes as the failure of the United States and Iran to reach a concrete peace agreement pushes countries in the region to diversify their defence partnerships and look beyond what experts described as an overreliance on Washington for their security. But they stress that closer cooperation does not mean abandoning long-standing alliances. Instead, the ambition is to gain greater control over their own security while strengthening pre-existing partnerships.

Arda Mevlutoglu, a defence industry analyst and managing director of Mergen Analytical Strategies, told Al Jazeera that the implications could extend well beyond the four participants.

“We may be witnessing the emergence of an interconnected network of defence and security arrangements extending from the Gulf to South and Southeast Asia, rather than a single formal alliance,” he said.

In a statement, the Qatari Defence Ministry said the “Badr” Memorandum of Understanding “aims to foster cooperation in the field of defence manufacturing, enhance defence capabilities among the four countries, and promote collaboration in technical defence training, as well as in research and development areas, thereby contributing to the creation of solutions and industries worthy of the evolution of modern defences”.

Experts say that under the agreement, each country will bring its own resources or set of skills to the table. “Turkiye contributes technological expertise, systems integration and a mature defence industry; Pakistan and Indonesia offer manufacturing capacity, skilled workforces and sizeable domestic markets; and Qatar provides investment potential and demand,” said Mevlutoglu.

Together, the four nations could “establish integrated supply chains, allowing these countries to jointly develop, manufacture and sustain defence systems”, he told Al Jazeera.

Such arrangements could give buyers a larger role in producing and supporting their own equipment, while providing manufacturers with longer-term orders and investment. Albert Vidal, a research associate at the International Institute for Strategic Studies, told Al Jazeera that Pakistan and Indonesia were both willing to purchase Turkish weapons and locate part of their production at home.

This could bring down costs for Turkish companies and bring jobs to Pakistan and Indonesia, while Qatar brings “financial depth”, he said.

Turkiye, home to one of the world’s most advanced defence sectors, already has military manufacturing ties with Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia separately. Qatar and Turkiye, for instance, signed a bilateral defence industry memorandum in October 2025.

But Vidal says that the new agreement, bringing together all four nations, points to a strategic calculation alongside an industrial one. Closer relationships could give more countries a stake in each other’s security. He pointed to Qatar’s investment in the Turkish defence industry over more than a decade and Ankara’s deployment of forces to Doha during the 2017 diplomatic crisis.

Pakistan’s existing naval manufacturing project with Turkiye, meanwhile, shows how weapons purchases can support domestic manufacturing. Of the four ships announced under the project, two are to be built in Istanbul and two at Karachi Shipyard.

Indonesia and Turkiye, meanwhile, are jointly building a tank.

“The rationale is to streamline these distinct defence export and joint production agreements under a more structured and resilient networked hub, rather than reinvent the wheel with each new defence agreement,” Burcu Ozcelik, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, told Al Jazeera.

The US-Israeli war with Iran and recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have heightened regional security concerns, analysts say, while reported US weapons shortages may be adding urgency to efforts to strengthen pre-existing partners and bolster domestic arms-building capacity.

“Diversification is a major driver, particularly as recent conflicts have exposed vulnerabilities associated with dependence on foreign suppliers, technology restrictions and supply chain disruptions,” Mevlutoglu said.

But he cautioned against interpreting the memorandum as a break with Washington. “Qatar is unlikely to abandon its strategic relationship with Washington, while Turkiye seeks greater technological independence within NATO, not autonomy from it,” he said.

According to Bader Mousa Al-Saif, an associate fellow with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme and an assistant professor at Kuwait University, the initiative reflects Gulf countries increasingly looking towards the Global South and fellow Muslim countries.

It also complements a separate effort to formalise military cooperation across the region, analysts say. Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August, establishing a mutual defence commitment. Ankara submitted the agreement to parliament for ratification on Wednesday, although deploying Turkish troops abroad would require separate parliamentary approval.

The Doha memorandum concerns industrial cooperation rather than a mutual defence pledge, but Mevlutoglu sees a connection between the two initiatives. “While Mecca focuses on collective deterrence and military cooperation, Doha could provide the industrial and technological foundations for such partnerships,” he said.

news.originalContent:
Experts warn that war takes a heavy toll on neurodivergent people, who often rely on routine.

Beirut, Lebanon – After her husband died from COVID-19 in 2020, Lena Kouyoumjian moved back to her parents’ house in Mazraat Yachouh, a village 20 minutes’ drive from Beirut. For Lena, energetic and outgoing, the move was difficult, but she accepted that she needed help to care for her 20-year-old daughter, Vana, who is autistic and non-verbal.

Lena first noticed her daughter’s symptoms when she was two years old. Vana is still unable to communicate verbally how she feels, but her mother does her best to understand her.

Like many autistic individuals – and neurodivergent people in general – Vana needs a supportive and stable environment, alongside a structured routine, to feel well.

Lebanon has been engulfed in war since October 2023, with bombings across the country and an economic crisis continuing to impact all Lebanese, particularly neurodivergent people.

When Israel escalated its attacks on southern Lebanon in March, as a trainer for children with disabilities, Lena understood that this could impact her autistic daughter.

“Any sudden change in routine, loud noises, fear, or uncertainty can increase their anxiety and make them feel unsafe,” Lena told Al Jazeera.

“I can see this in my daughter. Since the situation became more difficult, she has become more anxious and sensitive to the changes happening around her.”

The symptoms of autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) vary depending on the person and condition, but they frequently include sensory issues and emotional dysregulation. ADHD and autism often occur together, combining to make AuDHD, where traits from both conditions can be seen.

People with these neurodevelopmental conditions are often stigmatised by societies that do not fully understand them, including in Lebanon.

While the pressures caused by Israel’s war on Lebanon and mass displacement have led to psychological issues for many, neurodivergent people are more vulnerable due to their need for consistent support and routine.

“Being a parent of an autistic child isn’t something every parent can handle. A challenge I often face is deciding the amount of time and energy I should allocate to my child,” said Lena.

Lebanon’s Autism Awareness Association (AAA) has provided support for both mother and child. Vana has attended classes at AAA, a nonprofit based in Antelias, outside Beirut, for the past six years, which serves as an alternative school for young autistic people.

But rising costs in Lebanon during the war have prevented Vana from attending classes regularly. “Even transportation to her centre became very difficult, especially with the increasing financial challenges. At times, it became impossible for her to go, so she had to stay home,” Lena said.

Ghada Hayek Makhoul, who co-founded AAA with other parents of autistic children in 2015, said the group has made constant efforts to increase awareness about the condition in Lebanon.

“Many people don’t know what autism really is. They don’t know the spectrum; how it can vary from mild to moderate to severe,” Ghada told Al Jazeera.

Ghada’s son, Anthony, is a calm 27-year-old autistic, non-verbal man who relies heavily on helpers. Although he is unable to speak, his mother said it is clear when he is distressed, putting his hands over his ears when he is in pain due to sensory discomfort.

Autistic people can be more sensitive to noises than neurotypical people. During the war, people in Lebanon have been subjected to a harrowing range of sounds, from Israeli bombs exploding on the ground to the sonic booms of warplanes flying overhead.

“So, imagine the drones all the time [for autistic people], the bombs, and the vibration of the bombs … all of this that we were hearing, so of course it affected him a lot,” Ghada said.

“My son can’t listen to the TV any more due to the news. He switches it off and removes the remote control. It’s too triggering for him.”

Anthony’s mother said he senses tension and anxiety, even if his understanding of what is being said or happening is limited.

“[It affects] all the senses, everything. He doesn’t want to go into a pool any more. He used to love the water. And now, he doesn’t want to go into the pool any more,” Ghada said.

“I don’t know what changed. Because it’s outside? Because of the sound? I don’t know.”

Israel’s war on Lebanon has had a direct economic impact on the AAA and other organisations providing neurodivergent or psychological support.

Lebanon’s economic crisis, with inflation potentially reaching 17 percent this year, has also led to a brain drain of professionals who could support neurodivergent people.

AAA is a crucial support base for families with autistic children. But it comes at a significant cost of $700 per month for children attending five days a week. With 80 percent of the population living in poverty, few can afford such services.

“We need more trained staff, and we also need to keep the staff that are leaving the country. So, we need to have better salaries, but we cannot afford it, because we will have to increase the load on the parents,” said Ghada. “Things are in crisis mode for everybody during the war.”

The same thing is being seen with other mental health services. While many nongovernmental organisations (NGOs) provide free therapy, private consultations can cost more than $100 for a single 50-minute session.

Nour Toukan, a public health researcher at Enmaeya, a media platform focused on sustainable development, told Al Jazeera that care for people with autism or even for ADHD is “very much an out-of-pocket expense.”

While the government did launch a National Disability Allowance in 2023, with funding from the European Union and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), the allowance of $40 per month is not enough to cover even the basics in Lebanon. People with autism can get a personal disability card, issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs, making them eligible for support, but those with ADHD cannot.

Lebanon’s National Mental Health Programme, established in 2014 by the Ministry of Public Health, is trying to bridge gaps in support caused by economic and geographic variables.

Dr Rabih El Chammay, the founder and director of the programme, told Al Jazeera a national mental health strategy for children and teenagers is being finalised.

“National studies addressing autism and ADHD have also been conducted, providing evidence to inform this work. We are meeting with several organisations, particularly organisations representing families of persons with autism, to understand priorities and build momentum for further coordinated action,” Dr Rabih said. “War makes this work more difficult because it can increase support needs while disrupting the services people depend on.”

Displaced people have been the most impacted, but all of those in Lebanon whose schooling and routines have been disrupted are affected.

Adham Faraj, a 23-year-old psychology student at the Lebanese American University in Beirut, who was diagnosed with ADHD in 2024, said that when his classes moved online due to the war, he found himself staying at home more and more.

“It’s less engaging, especially if you struggle with attention. You’re less motivated to go out, so you just attend classes from bed,” Adham said.

Adham said the intensity of Israeli air strikes in Lebanon unsettled him, along with concerns about the rising price of medicine.

“There’s always a cheaper alternative, but it depends on people’s social class. Maybe an $11 box of medication is affordable for some, but not for everyone,” he said.

Rim Ajjour, a psychologist and psychotherapist in Beirut, whose work focuses on young people with autism, has seen that many of the skills neurodivergent people learned before the war are now being lost.

“With the limited resources available in Lebanon and the shift in people’s priorities, there has been more limited access to therapy,” she said.

Rim said that her clinic and others are doing their utmost to keep therapy accessible by freezing consultation fees, even when their own expenses are increasing.

With Israeli attacks continuing in southern Lebanon, which remains occupied by Israeli forces, in violation of a US-brokered June ceasefire, many fear the impact on their work in case of a return to full-scale war.

“I don’t know how we’ll be able to take it again,” Rim said.

news.originalContent:
The Israel Defense Forces’ (IDF) hotline intended for addressing instances of Israeli settler violence in the West Bank has been reportedly rendered nonfunctional.

Civilians, including journalists and diplomats have no reliable way to report settler violence, Israeli outlet Haaretz reported Monday. The issue was discussed by the High Court of Justice last Thursday, following a petition from the legal aid group Yesh Din.

Before the group of European diplomats were attacked by masked settlers on Saturday, a report concerning a violent group of Israeli settlers reached the operations room of the West Bank based Benjamin Brigade. However, the brigade did not respond, according to Haaretz. The Thursday petition came just days before settlers violently attacked both European diplomats and an American female journalist in the span of two days.

The operations room “is intended to receive reports from security personnel only, not civilians. It responds only to authorized personnel, who are not civilians”, the IDF Spokesperson’s Unit told Haaretz, “there are other centers designated to receive complaints from civilians.” (RELATED: Senate Blocks Dem-Led Resolution Calling For Israeli Settler Violence Probe)

The Israeli government did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment.

Heidi Levine, photojournalist for @wapo suffered serious injuries from vicious & cowardly attack. Heidi is US Citizen, clear ID as journalist. Details of who under investigation, but those who attacked unarmed reporter should spend YRS in prison. We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this. Attacking a female photographer is despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards. Dishonorable act of senseless violence.

However, civilians allege there is not a functional mechanism for reporting settler violence.

Previously, Palestinians could contact the Civil Administration’s “humanitarian cell,” before its discontinuation. Yesh Din and other legal aid organizations were told to direct urgent requests to the District Coordination and Liaison Office or IDF’s regional operations rooms, Haaretz reported. Soon after the 2023 Israel-Hamas War began, regional operations rooms began telling callers that they could not receive information from civilians. The Civil Administration hotline and the public inquiries officer of Central Command — two other military channels, operate for only several hours per day, open only Sunday through Thursday.

One of these hotlines directs callers to an email address. The other sparsely replies and its replies often amount to callers being told the hotline is unable to help. Palestinian phone numbers cannot call the police emergency hotline at 100, and there are often no Arabic speakers available, the outlet reported.

Additionally, police require IDF escorts into the areas with the heaviest concentration of settler violence. The Palestinian police force has no authority to address the issue, according to Haaretz.

After the High Court intervened in 2024, a hotline staffed by a single operator was established. However, the phone number was not made public to Palestinians. The state claimed it was working to improve its communication and response system. However, some military hotlines now play a voicemail saying they have been disconnected, Yesh Din alleges.

“The military commander found no reason to change the existing channels for reporting emergency incidents or to establish an additional way to contact a military official directly,” the state responded to the High Court per Haaretz.

The IDF is responsible for responding to reports from both settlers and Palestinians. However, without a feasible manner for them to receive complaints from non-settlers or security officials, they are only able to operate on the settlers’ accounts.

“The reason the distress calls from activists in the village of Taybeh were ignored is that the army’s operations room is willing to receive information about emergencies and respond to them only when settlers call,” Yesh Din attorney Roni Peli told Haaretz. “Palestinians, activists, journalists and diplomats have no way to call for help, and the army refuses to take responsibility for their security.”

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images)

Senate Democrats’ top campaign spending arm planned to spend $1.2 million in deep red Mississippi Tuesday while their candidate performed well in the polls.

The Senate Majority PAC intends to air the new television advertisement in support of Democratic Mississippi Senate nominee Scott Colom ahead of his race against Republican Mississippi Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, The Associated Press first reported. The ad is set to start Wednesday and air through Election Day.

“Senate Majority PAC has been watching this race closely, and it is clear Colom is running a competitive race that has put Hyde-Smith on her heels,” the PAC’s spokesperson Lauren French said.

Senate Majority PAC (D) announces its first spending in Mississippi It’ll start a $1.2 million TV ad campaign there Wednesday through Election Day, per an SMP spox #MSSEN

A Wedgwood Polls survey found Colom trailing Hyde-Smith 52% to 48%, while other polls found Hyde-Smith leading by single digits. Mississippi last elected a Democratic U.S. senator in November 1982 and both its Senate seats have been controlled by Republicans since 1989. (RELATED: Ranchers Say Trump’s Beef Imports Have GOP Senator Mike Rounds ‘Treading Water’ In South Dakota)

President Donald Trump won 60.9% of the vote in Mississippi during the 2024 presidential election.

Only $8 million has been spent in the Senate race, with Colom outspending Hyde-Smith nearly $4.6 million to $3.2 million, The Associated Press reported.

Colom campaigned with Democratic Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock and is scheduled to rally with former Vice President Kamala Harris on Thursday.

The Democratic candidate centered his campaign around affordability, which is the top issue for voters in the election cycle, according to his campaign website. He is also district attorney for Mississippi’s 16th Judicial District, giving him name recognition.

The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in May that Louisiana’s racially gerrymandered map was unconstitutional, prompting the Mississippi state Legislature considered redistricting to redraw black majority districts. The Mississippi state Legislature initially planned to redraw Mississippi’s lone majority-black district, although Republican Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves canceled a planned special legislative session on redistricting in May after receiving backlash from constituents.

Charles Taylor, executive director of the Mississippi state conference of the NAACP, said rising costs motivated Democratic voters across the state, according to The Washington Post. He highlighted how the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision mobilized black voters.

Thousands of protesters rallied in Jackson to protest the redistricting efforts and mobilized people to vote in November, according to Mississippi Today, a local outlet. Black voters make up roughly 35% of Mississippi’s voting population, according to The Washington Post.

The Senate Majority PAC launched a $5 million television ad campaign in Kansas, a state that has not had a Democratic senator since 1939. It also spent tens of millions in Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.

Democrats pulled spending from Georgia and North Carolina while Democratic Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff and former Democratic North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper held comfortable leads.

Republican PACs spent over $326 million to support Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton while he fell behind Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico. It spent $14 million to support Republican Kansas Sen. Roger Marshall and $5 million for Republican South Carolina Sen. Darline Graham.

Crowley’s signature appears on a series of contract approvals that increased Milwaukee Count

(Photo by Scott Olson/Getty Images)

Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial nominee David Crowley personally approved millions of dollars in county funding for his wife’s employer before seeking guidance from the Milwaukee County Ethics Board about another agreement, records reviewed by the Daily Caller show.

Crowley’s signature appears on a series of contract approvals that increased Milwaukee Count
news.originalContent:
(Photo by Scott Olson/Getty Images)

Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial nominee David Crowley personally approved millions of dollars in county funding for his wife’s employer before seeking guidance from the Milwaukee County Ethics Board about another agreement, records reviewed by the Daily Caller show.

Crowley’s signature appears on a series of contract approvals that increased Milwaukee County’s financial commitment to Community Advocates, a nonprofit employing his wife, Ericka Crowley, from $6.5 million to $17.85 million between 2020 and 2021.

Crowley, who became Milwaukee County Executive in May 2020, wrote to the Ethics Board in May 2021 about an upcoming rental assistance contract with Community Advocates, where his wife had begun working the previous year. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Dem Candidate Approved Tens Of Millions To His Wife’s Employer While In Office)

“Community Advocates was chosen as a community partner and vendor for the disbursement of Rental Assistance Funding due to the long-standing ties between Milwaukee County and their organization, their commitment to serving our communities, and their competency in administering vital programs like this one,” Crowley wrote in the letter reviewed by the Caller.

“My wife’s employment did not in any way influence the decision to award Community Advocates, and we have had many contracts with the organization — including a prior contract to disburse a previous tranche of Rental Assistance Funding — that were initiated and executed prior to my wife joining their organization as an employee,” he continued.

Crowley said he submitted the letter to maintain “full transparency.”

MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 06: Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Crowley is embraced by his wife Ericka following a campaign event

But while Crowley emphasized the county’s longstanding relationship with Community Advocates, records show he personally approved three increases to the nonprofit’s contract after his wife joined the organization.

Community Advocates originally received a $6.5 million contract in July 2020, just months after Crowley assumed office.

Crowley approved a $5 million increase on Nov. 25, 2020, bringing the contract’s total value to $11.5 million.

He approved another $950,000 increase on Jan. 12, 2021, bringing the total to $12.45 million.

On March 1, 2021, Crowley approved a third increase of $5.4 million, raising the agreement’s total value to $17.85 million and extending the contract through December 2021. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Dem Candidate Oversaw Contract With Soros-Linked Group Aimed At ‘Advancing Racial Justice’)

Crowley had previously disclosed his wife’s employment in an economic-interest statement received by Milwaukee County on Jan. 28, 2021, according to Wisconsin Public Radio.

But while that filing disclosed the financial relationship, it did not establish whether Crowley had sought ethics guidance on his personal involvement in approving funding for his wife’s employer.

Crowley had already approved two contract increases before the disclosure was received and signed off on another $5.4 million increase in March, more than two months before contacting the Ethics Board about an upcoming agreement.

In his May letter, Crowley said he had consulted Milwaukee County Corporation Counsel, which advised that the upcoming contract was permissible. The letter did not indicate whether he had obtained similar guidance before approving the earlier funding increases.

The county awarded the original contract without competitive bidding under emergency procurement procedures during the COVID-19 pandemic, Wisconsin Public Radio reported.

Crowley’s campaign told WPR, “Community Advocates launched their rent help program on April 1, before David was even County Executive.”

“When the county’s pandemic relief money came in, it plugged into the program that was already working, run by a partner the county had trusted for over two decades under Republicans and Democrats alike,” Crowley campaign spokesperson Philip Shulman said. “Every dollar was approved by the County Board in public, and David went above and beyond to disclose.”

Since Crowley assumed office in 2020, Milwaukee County distributed more than $65 million in federal Emergency Rental Assistance funds through its partnership with Community Advocates.

Crowley’s campaign did not respond to a request for comment from the Daily Caller.

Crowley will face off against Republican gubernatorial nominee and current Wisconsin Rep. Tom Tiffany in the general election on Nov. 3.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A Colorado town this week voted to install gates at its entrances in a bid to crack down on traffic passing through – but the move appears to have sparked a border war, with officials in nearby cities threatening to retaliate with a “nuclear option.”

Leaders in Bow Mar – a town of just 950 people – backed the idea after being stunned by the findings of a traffic study that revealed 1,200 vehicles were passing through the area daily, prompting them to act upon safety concerns flagged by residents.

Residents in Bow Mar, a town located 12 miles southeast of downtown Denver with properties averaging at $1.4 million, warned how the sheer volume of traffic posed a risk to kids playing outdoors and senior citizens, the New York Times reported.

Strategies such as a 20mph speed limit failed to deter out-of-town commuters from traveling through Bow Mar – a neighborhood that acts an alternative to drivers not wanting to navigate congestion between Denver and Littleton.

A plan to install gates at two of the town’s entrances and closing another entry point was touted over the summer – and there was a unanimous vote at a Monday council meeting.

The first gate could even be installed by Thanksgiving but it will not be in operation until January next year. It’s also unclear how the gate will be operated.

Bow Mar officials are convinced they’re acting on safety concerns and residents say the strategy isn’t motivated by a desire to seal off a community.

“I never wanted to live in a gated community,” Shane Fable, whose 12-year-old son was almost hit by a truck while he was changing a bike tire, told the Times. “It’s out of control.”

The truck smashed into a mailbox – and its driver was busted on a reckless driving charge and vehicular assault for driving while drunk.

Cops in the small town have issued more than 1,260 traffic tickets since the start of 2023 – half of which were for speeding offenses.

Officials in Littleton and Denver strongly believe the plan is counter-intuitive.

Furious Kevin Flynn, a Denver City councilman, has even speculated officials could retaliate – installing its own gate, something he has coined a “nuclear option,” according to the Denver Post.

“I think what they’re proposing is exacerbating our safety concerns by cutting off access to a public right of way to our residents,” Flynn told CBS.

“That’s not acceptable for us, for Bow Mar to be creating a significant traffic hazard for us in the course of resolving theirs.”

Kyle Schlachter, the Littleton mayor, and Mike Johnston, the Denver mayor, have even signed a joint letter calling on Bow Mar officials to pause their plans.

“Bow Mar undoubtedly expects its residents to have reasonable access to Denver and Littleton roads and rights-of-way,” the letter says.

“Denver and Littleton expect the same in turn.”

Schlachter claimed, “It’s hurtful when your neighbor says, ‘You’re not welcome in our community.'”

Amy Schumer shared a glimpse of her recent family vacation in Turks and Caicos, where she posed in a floral one-piece swimsuit before heading out on a scuba-diving excursion.

The 45-year-old comedian posted photos from her time at the beach resort, including several shots aboard a boat and footage of her exploring the ocean underwater.

In one photo, Schumer stood sideways on a boat, holding onto a metal railing as she looked over her shoulder toward the camera.

Her swimsuit featured pink roses and green leaves against a cream-colored background, with lace-up detailing along the back.

She completed the look with oversized tinted sunglasses, while her blonde hair was pulled into a casual ponytail.

Another image showed the “Trainwreck” star facing the camera in the same swimsuit, adjusting her sunglasses while holding a large orange buoy attached to a yellow rope.

Schumer also gave followers a glimpse of her underwater adventure, sharing footage of herself scuba diving in tropical waters.

“Our family had the time of our lives at @beachesresorts in Turks and Caicos,” Schumer captioned the Instagram post.

“2 best decisions of my life are becoming a mom and getting certified to dive by PADI,” she continued. “If you’re like me and have always wanted to dive, don’t wait!”

The actress, who shares 7-year-old son Gene with ex-husband Chris Fischer, also thanked the resort staff and credited TA3 for her swimsuit.Schumer’s vacation photos drew encouragement from several famous friends.

“Legs McGee. 🔥,” actor Cheyenne Jackson commented.

Actress Leslie Mann chimed in with “Babe,” while Lindsay Lohan and Krysten Ritter left heart emojis.

The tropical getaway also included some unexpected entertainment.

In an exclusive interview with People published Wednesday, Schumer recalled attending an impromptu wedding celebration after discovering a ceremony taking place on the beach near her family’s accommodations.

The comedian said she and Gene watched the vows from nearby lounge chairs before she joined the festivities and photobombed the newlyweds.

Schumer also described scuba diving as a highlight of the vacation, explaining that she had the opportunity to explore reefs and see a variety of fish.

Her son, meanwhile, enjoyed the resort’s water park, where the family spent time together during their stay.

The vacation comes as Schumer continues to share glimpses of her life following her weight-loss journey.

In December 2025, the comedian clarified that she had lost 50 pounds while addressing speculation about her changing appearance.

“I didn’t lose 30lbs, I lost 50,” Schumer wrote on Instagram at the time, which has since been deleted.

“Not to look hot which does feel fun and temporary. I did it to survive,” she continued.

Schumer, who previously revealed she had been diagnosed with Cushing syndrome, explained that her health had been a major factor in her physical transformation.

She also acknowledged using Mounjaro, a medication she had previously praised after experiencing severe side effects with another weight-loss drug.

In a since-deleted March 2025 Instagram video, Schumer said she had tried Wegovy several years earlier but struggled with nausea.

“Mounjaro’s been great,” she said, adding that she was having a positive experience with the medication.

Schumer has since emphasized that improving her health, rather than meeting outside expectations about her appearance, has been her priority.
