What the great mid-20th century theorist of anti-colonial resistance called “the wretched of the earth” are living in the downtrodden suburbs of Paris and, in effect, seeking to colonize the colonizers.

Make no mistake, though — white radicals, too, have taken a large hand in the disorder.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the leader of an ascendant left-wing party, has participated in the protests and condemned police for their supposedly brutish tactics.

He celebrates the “creolization” of France and views immigrants and their children as part of a potential “bloc de rupture” that can revolutionize French politics and shift it radically to the left.

What’s ultimately in play is French identity. The country has traditionally had a universalizing mission (whether advancing Christianity, or evangelizing for enlightenment values, depending on the regime) joined to an abiding love for the French nation.

Subscribe to our daily Post Opinion newsletter!

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

The rioters, who are illiberal and unpatriotic, aren’t much interested in either.

The unrest also serves as a warning that should the French public reject this vision and turn to the outré right winger, Marine le Pen, in next year’s national election, the country will be made ungovernable.

An element of de Gaulle’s “certain idea of France” was its inherent greatness.

His France, though, is already a second-rank power.

Its debt is 120% of GDP, while much of the public apparently believes it is living under intolerable austerity, and there is no political will to pull back on spending.

An overmatched President Emmanuel Macron, presiding over a restive and violent country, represents an exhausted center that has done much to bring the nation to this point.

Whatever the future of France, greatness is not likely to be part of it.

news.originalContent:

The young son of NFL Hall of Famer Eric Dickerson was allegedly called the N-word and subjected to vicious bullying and physical attacks by classmates at an elite California Christian school that charges nearly $48,000 a year in tuition, according to a new lawsuit obtained by the California Post.

Dickerson’s sixth-grade son (DD), who is black, was subjected to a year of racial harassment at Oaks Christian School during the 2024-2025 academic year — including being repeatedly called the N-word by classmates, compared to an animal and labeled with a racist nickname, according to the complaint filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court last week.

“His family repeatedly told Oaks Christian what was happening and asked the school to protect him,” Robert Glassman, the family’s attorney, told the California Post. “Instead of stopping the abuse, the school allowed it to continue.”

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

“No child should be subjected to racial harassment or physical violence at school while the adults entrusted with his safety fail to act,” he added.

The lawsuit accuses the posh Westlake Village school of negligence, intentional infliction of emotional distress and violating California’s Unruh Civil Rights Act.

“(DD) was a Black child who came to Oaks Christian School to learn and to grow. Instead, over the course of his sixth-grade year, (DD) was subjected to relentless racial harassment, bullying, and physical assault,” the lawsuit alleges.

One student repeatedly directed racial slurs at the sixth grader, including during a school-sponsored zoo field trip, where the student allegedly compared him to an animal, according to the complaint.

The same student who allegedly leveled the racist attack was also known to carry a knife on campus, yet school administrators imposed no discipline for the alleged harassment or the weapon, according to the lawsuit.

A female student allegedly struck (DD) in the head during lunch, took his food and deliberately poured out his water, according to the complaint. The school reviewed video and confirmed the assault had occurred, but merely spoke to the female student and told her not to do it again.

The most humiliating episode allegedly unfolded during music class, when students were discussing nicknames. The primary aggressor suggested calling (DD) “Ni–erson,” the lawsuit claims.

“When (DD) reported the ‘Ni–erson’ incident, his own teacher accused him of lying, in front of his peers,” the complaint states.

Oaks Christian is a private nondenominational Christian college-preparatory school which claims, “99% of its graduates are accepted into universities.”

New students in grades five through 12 can pay as much as $47,930 in annual tuition and fees, depending on the payment plan, according to the school’s official tuition and financial aid website. Returning students also face similar costs.

Oaks Christian did not respond to The Post’s request for comment.

Dickerson, 66, is one of the most prolific running backs in NFL history. Playing mostly for the Los Angeles Rams and Indianapolis Colts, he set the single-season rushing record in 1984 with 2,105 yards, breaking O.J. Simpson’s mark.

He was the first player to rush for more than 1,000 yards in seven straight seasons. When he retired in 1993, his 13,259 career rushing yards ranked second all-time. Dickerson was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1999.

The sixth grader’s famous father and his mother allegedly met with Vice Principal Tamara Kuku and proposed measures including speaking with students about racist language and contacting the parents of those responsible. The school failed to implement those measures, the lawsuit claims.

Dickerson’s son eventually withdrew from Oaks Christian and enrolled elsewhere, according to the complaint. He allegedly continues to suffer emotional and developmental harm from the alleged incidents.

The lawsuit also points to what it describes as a longstanding pattern of racism at the school.

In 2020, more than 8,100 Oaks Christian alumni signed a petition documenting alleged racism and discrimination experienced by black students over multiple years, according to the complaint.

The complaint also references ongoing litigation brought by another black former student who allegedly experienced racial slurs, a mock slave auction and threats of lynching while attending the school between 2021 and 2024.

The pricey private school has also produced NFL stars, including New York Giants linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux, Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet and Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr., as well as softball standout Maya Brady, niece of NFL legend Tom Brady.

The school has also attracted high-profile Hollywood families.

Its alumni include Sofia Richie Grainge, daughter of singer Lionel Richie; former “Bachelor” star Peter Weber; model Dree Hemingway, great-granddaughter of author Ernest Hemingway; Trey Smith, son of actor Will Smith; Nick Montana, son of NFL legend Joe Montana; and Trevor Gretzky, son of hockey great Wayne Gretzky.

news.originalContent:
US lawmaker says that government must arrest Israeli commander allegedly responsible for attack while he is in the US.

United States Representative Rashida Tlaib has called for her government to arrest the commander of an Israeli military unit believed to be responsible for the killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab in Gaza.

In a social media post on Monday, Tlaib pointed to reports that Israeli soldier Sean Glass was present in the US. She emphasised that the US had a legal responsibility to probe his involvement in Rajab’s death.

“As a party to the Genocide Convention and the Geneva Conventions, our government is obligated to arrest and investigate him for these war crimes and acts of genocide,” she wrote.

As part of her post, Tlaib shared a report from the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF), which tracks Israeli soldiers suspected of war crimes in Gaza.

The group said it has filed an emergency request for the US Department of Justice to arrest Glass.

“Sean Glass commanded the ‘Vampire Empire’ Company implicated in the killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab, members of her family, and the medics sent to rescue them. HRF’s investigation places him and his troops in the direct vicinity of Hind’s vehicle during the killing,” the group said in a statement.

“Today, Glass walks free in the United States. HRF demands that the US authorities arrest him and bring him to justice.”

The five-year-old’s killing on January 29, 2024, triggered global outrage and became a symbol of Israel’s targeting of Palestinian civilians and children during its genocidal war on Gaza.

Rajab and her family were attempting to leave Gaza City when their vehicle came under Israeli fire.

Her family was killed in the gunfire. Rajab called emergency services, appealing to rescuers, “I’m so scared. Please come!”

Recordings of her telephone call made international news. But both Rajab and the rescue team that tried to reach her were ultimately killed by Israeli forces.

The car Rajab was in was riddled with 335 bullet holes, which Israeli authorities initially blamed on a firefight with Palestinian fighters.

An investigation by the group Forensic Architecture found no evidence of an exchange of fire and concluded that only Israeli forces had been present in the area at the time of the incident.

Israel has opened a probe into the killings, but such investigations are seen by Palestinians as a means of dodging accountability and buying time until outrage over an incident dissipates.

Experts at the United Nations and other human rights watchdogs have declared Israel’s assault on Gaza to be a genocide. At least 74,000 Palestinians have been killed, including at least 21,000 children.

The US has continued to bolster Israel with diplomatic, military and economic assistance despite evidence of routine war crimes by Israeli forces in Gaza and elsewhere.

It has also denounced the International Criminal Court (ICC) for seeking the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant on charges of war crimes.

news.originalContent:
Hegseth has travelled to Israel to meet Netanyahu ahead of a closely contested election, Axios reported, citing sources.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an undisclosed visit to Israel, according to Axios.

The meeting between the hawkish ally of US President Donald Trump and the veteran Israeli premier facing a knife-edge election occurred on Monday, Axios reported, citing two sources with knowledge of the matter.

The Reuters news agency could not immediately confirm the visit. The Pentagon and Israel’s embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and there was no immediate indication of what they discussed.

President Trump took to his social media platform Truth Social on Sunday to endorse Netanyahu in next week’s parliamentary election, the first vote since the Hamas-led October 7 attacks in 2023 and Israel’s genocidal campaign in Gaza began.

Trump praised the prime minister for being an ally of the US in its war on Iran. He added that Netanyahu had his “Complete and Total Endorsement”.

“BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!” Trump wrote.

Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, although the opposition may also struggle to form a government, opinion polls suggest.

US Vice President JD Vance, however, declined to endorse Netanyahu in an interview earlier on Monday, saying he was not getting involved in Israeli elections.

“I endorse American candidates, and that’s where I’m focused on is the midterms,” Vance, who travelled to Budapest and endorsed Viktor Orban in Hungarian elections earlier this year, said in an interview with digital media outlet 2WAY.

“I’m not anti-endorsing him, but I’m not pro-endorsing him; I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections,” Vance said.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

When JJ Redick took over as the Lakers’ head coach in June 2024, he and Rob Pelinka, the franchise’s general manager and now president of basketball operations, laid out many emphases that fit into their vision of the franchise.

Among them was player development – with the exact phrase being mentioned by Redick and Pelinka at least 13 times during Redick’s introductory press conference on June 24, 2024.

Nearly 2 ½ years later, the Lakers’ player development system is coming back into focus after they waived 2024 first-round pick Dalton Knecht Monday to become compliant with the league’s rules, trimming their roster from 16 to 15 players signed to standard NBA deals.

The decision highlighted the Lakers’ struggles with maximizing younger players over the last few years.

If they are going to compete with the best of the Western Conference, led by the Spurs and Thunder, they must make a drastic improvement in this area.

Knecht, along with second-round pick Bronny James, who Redick once referred to as “case study one” for the franchise’s player development program after the team drafted the son of LeBron James with the No. 55 pick in the 2024 draft, made up the Lakers’ first draft class after Redick was hired.

The Lakers also had 2023 first-round pick Jalen Hood-Schifino and second-round pick Maxwell Lewis entering their second NBA seasons as Redick was brought on board.

But the Lakers have very little to show from the players in those draft classes.

Hood-Schifino? Traded to the Jazz, and immediately waived by Utah, as part of the three-team trade that brought superstar guard Luka Doncic to Los Angeles after an unremarkable 1 ½ seasons with the Lakers.

Lewis? Currently playing overseas after playing just 41 games for the Lakers, and two seasons in the NBA.

With Knecht now gone, Bronny is the Lakers’ lone draft pick from 2023 and 2024 still on the roster.

Even though he’s made significant strides in his development, to the point of being a positive contributor in the rotation toward the end of 2025-26 after regular-season, the younger James’ play during the preseason has made it clear he isn’t ready to be a regular contributor to this Lakers’ team.

There’s a good chance Reaves will not only be the lone player in the Lakers’ starting lineup on Wednesday who started his career with the franchise, but also the only player in the rotation who was at least on a rookie contract with the Lakers.

By comparison, the Thunder drafted three players projected to start this season (Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace) and traded for another (Shai Gilgeous-Alexander) while he was still on his rookie deal.

Even as those former young players sign more expensive veteran contracts, they have multiple young players on less expensive deals that will provide depth behind their higher-paid rotation players.

The Spurs are in a similar boat as the Thunder.

With the constraints on roster building under the first and second aprons, more attention and investments are being paid to identifying and developing younger players.

Even by the league’s best teams.

Pelinka spoke about this trend over two years.

“Part of the road to a really, really good team,” he said in June 2024, “and you can look around the landscape of the league right now with many young teams doing really, really well, is going to lean hard into that player development piece.”

It’s time for the Lakers to catch up in this department.

They must if they want to compete for a title while Doncic is in his prime.

The Thunder and Spurs, with their young stars and younger rosters, aren’t going anywhere.

Redick acknowledged developing second-year forward Adou Thiero and rookie wing Cameron Carr into “functional rotation NBA players over the next 12 to 24 months” would change the Lakers’ ceiling.

And he’s absolutely right.

The Lakers know firsthand how much quality development can change the direction of a franchise.

It’s why they’ve made hires and internal changes to ramp up their player development program over the last couple of years.

They developed Alex Caruso, who went undrafted in 2016 and joined the Lakers in 2017, into a rotation player for the 2020 title team before he departed the franchise in 2021.

Reaves developed from an undrafted player into a star guard who received a four-year, $180 million contract this past summer and is the unquestioned No. 2 option behind Doncic in this new era. He was also an essential part of the Lakers making the 2023 Western Conference finals.

Max Christie, the Lakers’ 2022 second-round pick, developed into a starting-level 3-and-D wing before being traded to the Mavericks as part of the Doncic acquisition.

But since then, the success stories haven’t come as often.

This needs to change if the Lakers want to have any shot at catching up with the best of the West over the next couple of years.

They must if they want to compete for a title while Doncic is in his prime.

The Thunder and Spurs, with their young stars and younger rosters, aren’t going anywhere.

Redick acknowledged developing second-year forward Adou Thiero and rookie wing Cameron Carr into “functional rotation NBA players over the next 12 to 24 months” would change the Lakers’ ceiling.

And he’s absolutely right.

The Lakers know firsthand how much quality development can change the direction of a franchise.

It’s why they’ve made hires and internal changes to ramp up their player development program over the last couple of years.

They developed Alex Caruso, who went undrafted in 2016 and joined the Lakers in 2017, into a rotation player for the 2020 title team before he departed the franchise in 2021.

Reaves developed from an undrafted player into a star guard who received a four-year, $180 million contract this past summer and is the unquestioned No. 2 option behind Doncic in this new era. He was also an essential part of the Lakers making the 2023 Western Conference finals.

Max Christie, the Lakers’ 2022 second-round pick, developed into a starting-level 3-and-D wing before being traded to the Mavericks as part of the Doncic acquisition.

But since then, the success stories haven’t come as often.

This needs to change if the Lakers want to have any shot at catching up with the best of the West over the next couple of years.

news.originalContent:
Ugandan police say a male body has been found in a village near Kampala, and his head has yet to be located.

An exiled vocal critic of the Rwandan government has been found decapitated near Kampala, south-central Uganda, according to a police spokesperson, in a case which remains under investigation.

Ugandan police said on Monday they were investigating the “murder of a male adult (around 50), whose head was cut off, and up to now, the head has not yet been recovered”, spokesperson Kituuma Rusoke told reporters, adding that the body had been identified by relatives as Robert Kabera.

The body was found in Luwala, a village near Kampala, and the killing likely took place late on October 16 or early on October 17, police added.

Robert Kabera, a former sergeant who fled Rwanda several years ago, was living in Uganda. The former soldier was not critical of the government during his time with the military, but grew increasingly opposed to Rwandan President Paul Kagame.

Kabera had a YouTube channel, “Major Robert TV”, with 144,000 subscribers. He featured a song praising opposition figure Victoire Ingabire, a rare voice of dissent in Rwanda who had been repeatedly imprisoned.

In Uganda, “Robert had no issues with anyone”, his brother, Victor Agaba, told the AFP news agency.

“Our problem comes from home… The army created a criminal case against him. It was a witch-hunt,” he said.

Kabera was declared a fugitive after leaving Rwanda and accused of corrupting a minor, charges he denied.

Rwandan authorities have been accused of assassinating opponents of President Kagame, who has governed the country since coming to power in 2000. The Rwandan president took the reins in the aftermath of the 1994 genocide in which 800,000 people were killed, primarily from the minority Tutsi community.

Kabera is not the first opposition figure in exile to be assassinated.

In 2021, a former lieutenant in the Rwandan army, Revocat Karemangingo, was shot dead in Mozambique, where he was suspected of secretly supporting an opposition force.

Outspoken opponent Seif Bamporiki was shot dead in South Africa the same year, while a former Rwandan intelligence chief turned critic, Patrick Karegeya, was strangled in his South African hotel room in 2014.

Former general Faustin Kayumba Nyamwasa, who co-founded the Rwanda National Congress (RNC) opposition party with Karegeya and lives in exile, has survived several assassination attempts.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

WASHINGTON — Ric Grenell, the embattled former executive director of the Kennedy Center, allegedly promised Turkish billionaire Turhan Mildon access to President Trump while reeling in an alleged $5.6 million donation to the performing arts venue that was never deposited.

The White House counsel’s office has been investigating Grenell for allegedly failing to provide the money to the center — after Mildon’s new bride, Alina Habba, directly told Trump during an Oct. 9 Oval Office meeting that her husband was duped into providing the funds.

“Once the money comes to the company here, I will arrange the donation to Kennedy Centre [sic], and you’ll be joining the VIP events and get close with the administration, even with POTUS,” Grenell allegedly wrote to Mildon in a May 3, 2025, text message first reported by Axios.

The $5.6 million donation allegedly was to be taken from a larger $17.6 million wire transfer from Mildon to the defense software company Texas Armament & Technology.

Grenell, a former US ambassador to Germany and Trump’s former acting intelligence director, reportedly denied sending the text message, pointing to the use of British English to spell “Centre.” He did not respond to The Post’s request for comment.

However, a Post source said that Axios’ recounting of the text message is consistent with what they had heard about developments in the bizarre scandal.

Mildon has provided the White House with financial records for a May 29, 2025, wire transfer to the Texas company for $17.6 million. However, Axios reported the money came not from Mildon, but from the Democratic Republic of Congo’s “Ministère des Finances.”

The business deal involved the central African nation, both Axios and the New York Times reported Monday, though neither outlet specified the nature of the venture in the vast country, where Mildon said in 2024 he operated limestone quarries and copper, cobalt and gold mines.

Mildon and Habba reportedly met early this year at the Kennedy Center, which Trump has sought to rebrand to include his own name. They were married on Sept. 26.

Habba previously worked for Trump as his personal attorney, then briefly at the White House before serving as acting US attorney in New Jersey.

Grenell and Mildon reportedly interacted on other matters involving Venezuela when Grenell served as a Trump envoy to then-Venezuelan President Nicholas Maduro. Mildon operates state-owned cement plants in the South American country.

After Maduro was captured by US troops on Jan. 3, interim president Delcy Rodriguez in June canceled Mildon’s contract to run those plants. The New York Times reported last week that Rodriguez paused her termination of Mildon’s contract after learning of his relationship with Habba.

news.originalContent:
Lawyers for the former student leader seek to overturn an appeals court decision that would allow for his removal.

Pro-Palestine activist Mahmoud Khalil has petitioned the United States Supreme Court to review a court ruling that could pave the way for his re-arrest and deportation.

On Monday, Khalil’s lawyers filed an emergency application to the high court, seeking an immediate stay of a decision from Philadelphia’s 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals.

That court had ruled that federal law should have prohibited lower courts from ordering Khalil’s release from immigration detention in June 2025.

Instead, the appeals court said that Khalil’s detention should have been weighed first in an immigration court — a system overseen by the executive branch of the US government — and not in district court, which is part of the judicial branch.

In March 2025, Khalil became the first student protester known to be targeted for his pro-Palestinian views under the second administration of President Donald Trump.

A permanent US resident and former Columbia University graduate student, Khalil was arrested inside the student housing complex where he lived with his wife, a US citizen.

The push to deport Khalil has become a flashpoint in the debate over free speech on US campuses.

His petition to the Supreme Court could result in a major legal showdown that determines whether federal courts can intervene when noncitizens face retaliatory detention for speech protected under the First Amendment of the US Constitution.

Khalil’s lawyers have asked the Supreme Court to rule that noncitizens do indeed have the right to sue if immigration officials detain them as a reprisal for exercising free speech.

“If the Trump administration can punish someone for their pro-Palestine speech, this or any future administration can punish anyone for any speech,” Khalil said during a news conference on Monday.

Trump campaigned for re-election in 2024 in part on a pledge to crack down on the pro-Palestinian student protest movement, which had erupted in 2023.

Columbia University in New York became an epicentre for such activism. Khalil, who was born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria, had served as a spokesperson for the protest groups.

The Trump administration, however, has characterised pro-Palestinian activism as a threat to US foreign policy interests. It has argued it has the legal right to deport noncitizens who engage in such protests as a result.

After his arrest, Khalil was quickly moved to immigration detention centres in New Jersey, then Louisiana, where he remained in custody for more than three months.

Khalil faces deportation to Algeria or Syria if the 3rd Circuit Court’s decision holds.

In May, the 3rd Circuit narrowly voted six-to-five against reconsidering his case, but its decision will not go into effect until Khalil has exhausted his appeals.

He has fought his deportation both in the immigration court system and in the federal district court system, where he has filed a habeas corpus case. Both cases remain ongoing.

In April, the Board of Immigration Appeals denied his appeal in the immigration court system and issued a final order of removal in his case.

On Monday, faculty and staff at Columbia University held a silent vigil outside one of the school’s gates to protest what they described as “abducted students”, taken by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Placards with portraits of Khalil and fellow student protester Mohsen Mahdawi, among others, were hoisted into the air. Demonstrators called for solidarity with the students facing deportation and pushed for Columbia University to reopen its gates to the public after their closure during the protest movement.

news.originalContent:
The collapse of an illegal gold mine in southwestern Colombia killed 14 people and injured seven others, local authorities said on Monday.

The accident took place in the rural Chambero sector of the Santa Barbara de Iscuande municipality, located in the department of Narino.

Search and rescue operations have concluded, Narino Governor Luis Alfonso Escobar said.

Jorge Tovar Castillo, a disaster response official in Narino, said that an additional 12 to 15 miners have been reported as missing following the accident.

He said that municipal authorities were handling the response but added that communication had been difficult.

Santa Barbara de Iscuande is surrounded by dense rainforest and can only be reached by boat or small aircraft.

In a message on X, Escobar said the gold mine was an “informal” mine.

Informal and unregulated mining is common in rural parts of Colombia, where operations often lack adequate safety infrastructure, leading to frequent fatal accidents.

“At this moment our priority is to save lives, accompany families and guarantee an opportune response to this painful tragedy,” Escobar wrote.

In August, 13 people died in a similar mining accident in the municipality of Policarpa, also in Narino.

news.originalContent:
Tehran summons envoy in tit-for-tat move after Berlin summoned ambassador to Iran.

Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has summoned Germany’s ambassador after a court in Hamburg found two men guilty of plotting to kill two leaders of Jewish organisations at Tehran’s behest, accusing Berlin of leveling “baseless political allegations”.

The decision to summon envoy Axel Dittmann came after Germany summoned the Iranian ambassador, Majid Nili Ahmadabadi, on Monday over allegations that Tehran was behind the plot to assassinate the two pro-Israel public figures.

“Levelling security-related accusations against Iran has long been a tactic employed by the Zionist regime and certain Western nations,” Iran’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement broadcast by official news agency IRNA.

“Attempting to provide a judicial face to baseless political claims not only fails to lend any credibility to such allegations but also undermines the standing of the German judiciary itself,” the statement added.

Berlin’s allegations stem from a court case involving two men, a Danish national and an Afghan national, who were convicted in a Hamburg court on Thursday for planning to target the president of Germany’s main group representing the Jewish community and the head of the German-Israeli society.

The German Foreign Ministry said on X that the Iranian ambassador had been summoned, adding Tehran would not be allowed to “threaten our free society”.

“The malicious assassination attempts against Josef Schuster and Volker Beck will have legal consequences,” it added.

“We do not tolerate attacks on Jewish life and on those who defend it anywhere, and certainly not in Germany.”

The Dane, partially identified as Ali Hassan S, was jailed for eight-and-a-half years. The Afghan, who was recruited as his accomplice, was sentenced to four-and-a-half years.

Iran’s intelligence service steered the two men, the court said. The pair were arrested in Denmark last year and extradited.

In sentencing the men, the judge said they were guilty of “terrorist activities orchestrated by Iran”.

At the time they were charged, the Iranian embassy in Berlin released a statement rejecting what it called “unfounded allegations made at the behest of Iran’s enemies”.

“Real Housewives” star Carole Radziwill insisted Monday that she’s a hard-nosed parking enforcer in her SoHo neighborhood  — even as she’s racked up thousands of dollars in tickets herself.

Radziwill, 63 — who recently revealed on her reality TV show that she tries to dodge the city’s real-life parking enforcers with her own traffic cones — told Page Six’s “Virtual Reali-Tea” that she can’t tolerate people who don’t abide by the city’s alternate-side street-cleaning routine.

“I’m the one who, if people are sitting in their car and they don’t pull out, I will bang on their window and be like, ‘No, no, you’re not just sitting here. You gotta move because we need the streets clean,’ ” she said, referring to the  much-maligned New York ritual requiring drivers to move their cars for an hour and a half twice a week to make way for street sweepers.

Radziwill — who has also used an expired FDNY placard in her windshield to dodge the rules — racked up $8,000 in traffic violations since 2020, including 17 tickets for missing alternate side street cleaning.

But she touted that record to bolster her bona fides as a parking-enforcement hero.

“Thank you New York Post for doing the research. I only had 17 alt-sides tickets. That is like legend status.” she said. “Over six years, that’s three a year.

“Find someone who has a better record than that,” she added.

The reality star’s parking tactics landed her on the cover of The Post on Friday after she bragged in a recent “Real Housewives of New York’’ episode about keeping the ConEd cones in her car to plop on the roof and trick meter maids into not ticketing her.

“The cone is a cop family hack. If I’m parked illegally or slightly too close to a hydrant, they will keep on walking,” she said.

That wasn’t just reality-show bluster — Radziwill’s red Jeep Cherokee had two orange ConEd cones stashed in the trunk when The Post tracked it down last week, along with a long-expired FDNY parking placard taped under the windshield.

And the housewife — who was married to the late Anthony Radziwill, nephew of Jackie Kennedy — stood by her parking practices after the expose.

“I’ll never change the way I park,’’ she said Monday.

“I think people think it’s like a money thing, that I don’t want to park it in the garage because they’re expensive,” she said. “It absolutely isn’t, it’s not.

“I would not have a car in the city if it was in a garage because I use my car. Almost every day I use it.”

She also noted she was fully paid up on her traffic fines — and that it was still cheaper to eat the fines rather than pay for a garage, which in SoHo runs around $800 per month.

“Eight thousand dollars is by the way nothing, it’s $100 a month over the six years because parking is expensive in the city,” she said.

By comparison, paying for a garage at $800 a month over that time would cost nearly $60,000.

But Radziwill insisted she doesn’t try to game the system — and loathes anybody who does.

“Those people, they don’t move their car usually and they don’t care about the ticket,” she said. “I don’t like that.”

“I love the city. I love my car. I love freedom of having that car right outside my door,” she added. “And as the New York Post has shown, I’m really f–king good at alt sides, OK? There you are.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Polymarket caved to backlash and removed a bet that allowed gamblers to wager on whether seven Cornell University fraternity members accused in a gang-rape lawsuit will face felony sex-crime charges.

The company took down the wager after activists demanded that LeBron James and other celebrity endorsers cut ties with the prediction-market platform

More than $450,000 had been traded on the wager as of Monday afternoon as authorities revisited allegations that a female student was drugged and sexually assaulted at a fraternity house in 2024.

Before the bet was removed, traders were pricing the probability of felony charges against at least one of the men at roughly 28%, with $451,633 in trading volume.

News of the wager, which was available on Polymarket’s international platform but not its US app, was first reported by Front Office Sports.

Polymarket took the page for the bet offline after The Post contacted the company seeking comment.

The betting frenzy sparked outrage among sexual assault advocates, who pressured the company’s high-profile celebrity pitchmen to denounce the market publicly.

“This is dehumanizing, disgusting, and dangerous,” attorney Cheyenne Hunt wrote in an Instagram post.

“To the celebrity ambassadors for Polymarket, do you really want to be associated with this?” she added.

A petition circulating online under the banner “No Gambling on Gang Rape!” singled out James, Eli Manning, Derek Jeter, Emily Ratajkowski, Alexandra Daddario and other celebrities who have promoted the platform.

The Post has sought comment from those celebrities.

The campaign accused the stars of lending their reputations to a company that permits speculation on sexual assault cases and urged them to sever their relationships with Polymarket.

“As women, sexual assault survivors, advocates, and allies, we are horrified that this type of betting is not only being allowed,” the petition states.

The organizers also warned that allowing people to profit from the outcome of criminal proceedings could create financial incentives for individuals with influence over a case to interfere with the process.

There is no known evidence that such interference has occurred in the Cornell investigation.

The controversy threatens to put Polymarket’s lucrative celebrity marketing strategy under scrutiny.

James is receiving $15 million annually to promote the company, Front Office Sports reported last month.

“Endorsing an exchange is different from endorsing a sneaker, because the product is the set of questions the company chooses to ask, so endorsers should know what categories are off limits and have an exit when the platform crosses a line,” Alex Goldenberg, a senior fellow at Rutgers University’s Miller Center for Community Protection and Resilience, told The Post.

Other prominent endorsers include former NFL stars Manning, Reggie Bush and Richard Sherman, along with basketball legend Sue Bird.

Representatives for the athletes did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The advocacy group I Have The Right To, which focuses on sexual assault, also condemned the wager and accused celebrities of helping legitimize the platform.

“What kind of culture looks at sexual violence and sees an opportunity for profit?” the nonprofit asked in an Instagram post.

Polymarket defended its decision to offer the contract, arguing that prediction markets provide valuable information about major events.

A company spokesperson told Front Office Sports that such markets can offer “objective, data-driven insight into how a matter like this is moving through the legal system.”

The spokesperson added that sexual assault on college campuses deserves greater transparency and public attention.

“Polymarket says these markets simply reflect what participants believe, but the platform has built a financial incentive structure that rewards anyone with inside knowledge of a case or a hand in steering it, from investigators to grand jurors to witnesses,” Goldenberg told The Post.

Goldenberg is an adviser to BETINT, a company that monitors prediction markets for suspected insider trading and manipulation. He said he has no financial ties to Polymarket or rival Kalshi.

The uproar centers on a civil lawsuit filed Sept. 16 in Manhattan Supreme Court by a woman identified as Jane Doe, who alleges that seven members of Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity sexually assaulted her during the night of Oct. 19, 2024, and into the following morning.

According to the 101-page complaint, the then-20-year-old student was intoxicated when she arrived at the frat house, where members allegedly supplied her with ketamine, marijuana and additional alcohol before subjecting her to repeated sexual assaults.

The lawsuit names Cornell, several fraternity and sorority organizations and the seven men, accusing the university and other defendants of failing to protect the student.

The allegations have not been established in court.

The Tompkins County district attorney initially declined to bring criminal charges in 2024 but has since reopened the investigation.

Cornell has said its disciplinary proceedings resulted in sanctions that included suspensions and expulsions.

Two sacred Catholic relics — including a cloth stained with the blood of the 13th century saint and an Italo-Byzantine style painted panel that once covered his tomb — are now on display at St. Mary’s Cathedral of the Assumption after leaving Italy for the first time.

The bloody cloth, encased in a silver reliquary, is linked to one of the most famous mystical encounters recognized by Catholics.  After 40 days of fasting, St. Francis of Assisi — the Italian friar, animal lover and patron saint of San Francisco — is believed to have received the holy stigmata, or spontaneous bleeding representing the crucifixion wounds of Jesus Christ,  on La Verna in Italy, using the crude bandage to stanch the blood.

Rarely seen remains of the beloved friar were publicly displayed this year at the Basilica of Saint Francis in Assisi, Italy to mark the 800-year anniversary of the saint’s death, a special jubilee year declared by Pope Leo XIV.

The San Francisco display was organized with the help of the Knights of Saint Francis of Assisi, a Catholic lay organization founded by attorney and former politician Angela Alioto, to celebrate the jubilee year of their namesake saint.

“Again, these relics have not left italy in 800 years, and they won’t be back anytime soon. So please do the best you can and getting over to see this incredible little museo,” Alioto wrote on social media. It’s considered a “second class” in the Catholic Church, or an item belonging to a saint— as opposed to direct remains, like the fragmented kneecaps and ribs of St. Bernadette Soubirous that are also touring the US this year. The Catholic tradition of venerating relics dates back to 156 A.D.

The other relic is a full-length image of Saint Francis is traditionally attributed to Italian painter Cenni di Pepo, and features a golden rendering of the famed saint. In the image, Francis stands in the simple brown habit of the Friars Minor with a golden halo, a book, and the stigmata wounds. Additional art pieces on display include Painting of the Veil of St. Clare of Assisi; Renaissance paintings by Dono Dori, The Stigmata of St. Francis and Crucifixion of St. Francis of Assisi; St. Francis Watched Over by the Angels by an anonymous 17th century painter; and St. Francis by Adamo di Cladaro.The relics will be on display through Nov. 28.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Steve Hilton is demanding federal officials turn over records — including a former federal contractor’s laptop — that he claims could expose what Xavier Becerra knew about migrant children being handed to traffickers during the Biden administration.

The Republican candidate for governor is targeting his Democratic rival’s tenure as Health and Human Services secretary, alleging Becerra and the Biden White House knew children were being delivered to sex and labor traffickers.

In a letter sent Monday to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Hilton pointed to a former federal contractor’s laptop that he said had been given to congressional investigators.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

The letter identified the whistleblower as Tarek “Joey” Kadourah, who supervised a transportation team for federal contractor MVM that moved migrant children from government facilities to sponsors.

“If the testimony of whistleblowers is accurate, and the contents of the laptop are as reported, the role of Xavier Becerra and the Biden White House in the trafficking of thousands of migrant children represents one of the biggest and most shocking scandals in U.S. government history,” Hilton wrote.

Hilton’s campaign reported $406.10 in car service and meal expenses for Kadourah’s travel for interviews in August, according to a campaign finance disclosure.

In a recent interview with journalist Lara Logan, Kadourah alleged agents reported children crying, girls trying to flee during transportation stops and adults with apparent gang tattoos collecting children.

“Some of them even looked like gang members,” Kadourah said, citing what he described as “MS-13 tattoos, Mexican mafia tattoos.”

He recalled a military veteran and former corrections officer raising concerns after two men with prison tattoos arrived to collect a child. Kadourah said he repeatedly alerted his supervisor, only to be told: “Hey, they’ve been vetted. Everything’s OK. Keep your mouth shut. Just keep doing the job.”

Hilton wrote that Kadourah’s laptop “apparently contains evidence” that Becerra and the Biden White House knew children were being transported by the government directly to traffickers.

The letter does not include specifics about the laptop’s records or establish that investigators substantiated Kadourah’s allegations.

Hilton also wrote that his campaign had been informed that Homeland Security Investigations was examining the matter, “including specifically the role of Xavier Becerra.” The letter offers no independent confirmation of that assertion.

“It’s sad to watch Trump’s chosen candidate Steve Hilton be consumed by his own desperation,” Jonathan Underland, a spokesperson for the Becerra campaign, told The Post in a statement.

“Nothing is working, so he’s inventing Q-Anon brainrot to distract from a weak policy platform that would make billionaires richer and hurt working families.”

The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Citing border czar Tom Homan, Hilton said approximately 140,000 children remain unaccounted for. The letter does not establish how many were confirmed missing rather than unreachable through government follow-up efforts. Hilton also wrote that some children placed in dangerous situations had died.

John Fabbricatore, a senior adviser for the Trump administration at HHS’ Office of Refugee Resettlement, told The Post in August that investigators had found more than 40 migrant children dead, though some had since become adults: “We found kids in sex trafficking. We found kids who were murdered, kids who were in slave labor.”

Hilton’s letter follows additional reporting by The Post in which a former Biden administration official accused Becerra of referring to migrant children as “little Juanitos and Juanitas” while leading HHS. Becerra denied using that language about migrant kids, and Underland defended Becerra’s leadership of HHS by noting, “Jealousy breeds contempt.”

Hilton urged Mullin to work with current HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and congressional investigators to establish what Becerra knew and how he responded to warnings from staff and contractors.

“Becerra is now asking the people of California to make him their governor,” Hilton wrote. “They deserve to know the truth about what he did before they cast their votes.”

news.originalContent:

WASHINGTON — House Speaker Mike Johnson revealed that he privately pushed the White House to contemplate the consequences of giving Russia sanctions relief as its bloody war in Ukraine unfolds.

Last week, President Trump halted the implementation of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which came on the heels of him easing certain sanctions on Russian diesel.

“We understand that Putin cannot be trusted. He demonstrates that over and over and over,” Johnson (R-La.) told Fox News’ “Sunday Morning Futures.”

“I told the White House team that we need to talk about it, and I think carefully consider the unintended consequences that may ensue from that,” he added. “So I know the president’s evaluating this, as he does everything else.”

Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel to flow into the US and pause the implementation of new secondary sanctions drew bipartisan blowback.

Top administration officials have pointed out that several European countries have imported fuel from Russia and contended that the secondary sanctions would impact US relations with countries that do business with Russia.

“The only thing that has been lifted is the diesel embargo. And, you know, I will point out the UK in May waived their embargo on diesel and jet fuel made with Russian crude,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday.

High diesel prices have caused midterm headaches for Trump, particularly due to farmers’ reliance on it.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright theorized that the sanctions relief could motivate Russia to “tone down” the war in Ukraine due to a desire to keep up the diesel exports.

Trump similarly argued in a Truth Social post that he doesn’t “want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.”

Johnson also acknowledged that some of his colleagues had concerns about Ukrainian accusations that the Trump administration throttled its access to Starshield satellite internet and hasn’t been sharing intelligence about incoming Russian ballistic missile strikes.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) revealed Monday that he co-hosted a call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who expressed concerns about Starshield and intelligence sharing.

“Unquestionably, we stand with Ukraine against Russia’s murderous invasion,” Blumenthal posted on X. “Ukraine wants peace & is ready to negotiate—appeasement won’t work with Putin, a thug who understands only strength & force.”

THREAD: Joined Senator Tillis today to host an update from President Zelenskyy with bipartisan colleagues—hearing from him highly alarmingly that intelligence sharing & Starshield access are still partially degraded. 1/

Officials such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio have denied that the Trump administration ordered a slowdown on Ukraine’s Starshield access or cut off intelligence sharing.

“I don’t know who it was, but I’d like to find out,” Trump said when asked about that Monday. “Zelensky is a man that should have had this war settled a long time ago.”

“Ukraine could have had this thing settled a long time ago. If he would have listened to me, and you remember the Oval Office, he would have had this settled a long time ago. Maybe it’s time for Zelensky to get somebody else to negotiate.”

Hunter Schafer revealed she underwent bottom surgery in December 2025.

The “Euphoria” alum, 27, discussed undergoing the operation to change a person’s genitals to align with their gender identity in an interview with Elle magazine published Monday. She called the surgery “amazing” and noted, “I love it so much.”

Schafer said that she’s struggled with the tension between queerness as an idea and philosophy “versus how it applies and works in real life, in the context of the world that we’re living in.”

Ultimately, gender-affirming surgery was  the right decision for the actress, who began transitioning when she was 14 years old.

“For a long time I’ve embraced the gender-expansive part of myself, and I really wanted to try to make that previous body work, because I thought there was something really cool and badass about it,” she reflected.

But at this point, she feels no ambiguity about her gender identity.

“I’m a woman. I’m a girl,” she said.

Back in 2024, Schafer talked about not wanting to be pigeonholed when it comes to being transgender.

“I don’t want to be [reduced to] that, and I find it ultimately demeaning to me and what I want to do,” she told GQ magazine. “Especially after high school, I was sick of talking about it. I worked so hard to get to where I am, past these really hard points in my transition, and now I just want to be a girl and finally move on.”

She added, “It’s a privilege, but it’s been very intentional. I’ve gotten offered tons of trans roles, and I just don’t want to do it. I don’t want to talk about it.”

Her stance appears to have softened, as she told Elle in her new interview that she would be love to star in a “trans girl rom-com.”

“I’ve been thinking about that for a while,” she said. “I would like to make that happen.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

American black bears are wreaking havoc in California’s famous Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks, smashing through campsites, raiding dumpsters, and driving up property damage figures as they enter a pre-hibernation feeding frenzy.

Official National Park Service figures reveal bear-related incidents have skyrocketed by a staggering 125% since 2020.

More alarmingly, total property damage costs have exploded by an unprecedented 1,800 per cent year-to-date, surging to $17,358 compared to a modest $898 just six years ago.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Park records show total incidents rose from 158 in 2020 to 356 by late September 2026.

The surge comes as hundreds of black bears roam the 1,353-square-mile park grounds, actively foraging for massive caloric intake before entering winter dens between October and December.

While the sprawling parks welcome more than 1.5 million tourists annually, rangers are warning holidaymakers that human negligence is fueling the chaos.

Up to late September, 61 recorded incidents involved unsecured rubbish dumpsters and bins, while 19 involved bears snatching food straight out of campsites, picnic sites, and vehicles.

The wildlife crisis has proven fatal on park roadways as well.

Areas like Giant Forest, Halstead Meadow, and Cedar Grove have emerged as dangerous collision hotspots, with 18 bears injured in vehicle strikes since 2020 and four killed.

In 2024, park staff were forced to euthanase a severely injured bear cub following a hit-and-run impact.

Park authorities noted that fluctuating visitation patterns—driven by past pandemic closures, wildfire disruptions, and recent winter mudslides—have heavily impacted human-bear interactions over the seven-year tracking period.

Over that span, six problem bears have been euthanased due to conflict behavior, while two human injuries have been documented.

Park Superintendent Woody Smeck urged tourists to practice strict vigilance when visiting the pristine Sierra Nevada wilderness.

“Black bears in our national parks are wild, beautiful animals,” Mr Smeck said. “We ask visitors to admire them from a safe distance and to secure food and other scented items.”

Officials advise anyone confronted by a aggressive or bluff-charging bear to stand their ground, raise their arms to appear larger, and shout loudly, warning visitors never to run or place themselves between a mother and her cubs.

news.originalContent:
A Reuters/Ipsos poll reveals Democrats are leading by 12 points in generic US congressional ballot surveys against Republicans.

United States President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 31 percent – another record low in his political career, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll.

The same poll found Trump’s Republican Party also at a major disadvantage: when respondents were asked whether they would rather vote for a generic, unnamed Democrat or Republican, Democrats led by 12 points.

The percentage of Americans who disapprove of Trump has grown steadily in recent months, especially since the February 28 launch of the US-Israel war on Iran, which has driven up petrol and diesel prices and had knock-on effects across the economy.

Several recent polls have documented the growing problems facing Trump and his party ahead of midterm elections, set for November 3, which could determine control of the House and Senate.

An NBC poll released Sunday found 71 percent of Americans said the country was on the “wrong track” and 55 percent would vote for the Democratic Party if an election were held that day.

A Washington Post/ABC/Ipsos poll, also released on Monday, found Trump had a record-low approval rating of 33 percent, with 7 out of 10 saying petrol or gasoline was becoming unaffordable.

news.originalContent:
First Lady Melania Trump has championed the executive action as a ‘transformative moment’ for US women’s health.

United States President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that will establish a dedicated women’s health division within the National Institutes of Health (NIH), as well as a White House task force focused on the subject.

During a signing ceremony in Washington on Monday, First Lady Melania Trump praised the initiative as setting “a new standard for women’s health in America”.

“This is a transformative moment for women in America. Beginning today, we will change the reality of women’s health,” she said.

“Previous generations fought for women’s rights. Our generation will fight to discover the cures that will ensure a woman can live her life in health and to the fullest.”

The newly minted project, spearheaded by the first lady, requires the new health division to be established within 90 days.

It aims to accelerate scientific discoveries, expand clinical access for women’s health and modernise care throughout every stage of a woman’s life.

The new division at the NIH will not replace the agency’s Office of Research on Women’s Health but will have a broader mandate beyond research, according to the White House.

Melania Trump gestured to “super intelligence, advanced biotechnology and groundbreaking therapies” as tools that offer a “unique chance to reinvent women’s healthcare”.

The first lady’s office has identified “five pillars” for innovation in the field. One involves funding targeted research to develop cures for diseases that affect women, such as endometriosis.

Another calls for a quicker timeline for “promising therapeutics” to reach female patients.

“In 2026, medical advances can do more than just prolong life,” said Melania Trump. “It should give women the freedom to live life to its fullest, to pursue our dreams, experience love, discover, create, travel and lead.”

The White House task force will be co-chaired by the newly cancer-free White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, as well as Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr.

While Monday’s executive order mandates that the HHS must fund the administrative costs of the task force, the order itself does not include any specific funding targets or dollar amounts.

Experts have noted that Melania Trump has kept a relatively low profile during Trump’s second term.

Her public appearances have been fewer than during Trump’s first term, though she has stepped into the public spotlight to promote improvements to foster care and the role of technology, such as artificial intelligence in education.

During Trump’s first term, the first lady launched the “Be Best” campaign focused on child well-being, safe social media and countering opioid abuse.

But critics have questioned how effective Monday’s executive order might be, given the cuts Trump has made to the federal workforce since his second inauguration.

Thousands of employees have been laid off at the NIH alone, with Kaiser Health News reporting that its workforce is at its lowest level in decades.

The NIH was also given a deadline to slash spending by 35 percent across all of its divisions, amounting to a massive $2.6bn budget reduction.

In April 2025, the HHS drew widespread condemnation and a multi-state lawsuit after abruptly moving to terminate regional contracts for the Women’s Health Initiative, the nation’s largest longitudinal study on older women’s health at the time.

Critics warned that the move would jeopardise life-saving research on cardiovascular disease, cancer and osteoporotic fractures for senior women.

news.originalContent:
Helsinki recently joined regional peers in withdrawing from the UN Charter banning munitions as it eyes its eastern border.

Finland is seeking to acquire one million anti-personnel mines.

The plan to spend 100 million euros ($112 million) on the munitions comes after Helsinki and regional peers withdrew from a United Nations compact rejecting their use.

With Moscow increasingly accused of mounting hybrid warfare against supporters of Ukraine, and possibly planning military provocations, Finland exited the Ottawa Convention last year.

Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland, all also among the staunchest allies of Ukraine, also quit the agreement, citing the potential threat from Moscow.

Colonel Riku Mikkonen of the Army Command told Finland’s national news agency STT that officials are now gathering information from suppliers regarding the deal, the AFP news agency reports.

Helsinki would like domestic manufacturers to supply the mines, with contracts signed by the end of 2027 and production up and running by 2028.

“It would be useful in many ways if Finnish companies produced the anti-personnel mines in Finland,” Mikkonen said. About half a dozen Finnish firms qualify, he told STT.

“However, at this stage, buying the mines from abroad is not totally ruled out,” he added.

Finland joined the Ottawa Convention, a humanitarian treaty aimed at eliminating anti-personnel landmines and destroying more than a million of them, in 2012.

However, it announced that it was withdrawing in April 2025, citing a worsening security climate, and stopped being bound by the treaty in January.

Prime Minister Petteri Orpo has called Russia, which sits on Finland’s eastern edge, a long-term threat.

Finland shares a border of roughly 1,340 kilometres (830 miles) with Russia. It has beefed up its defences since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and reported that migrants have been pushed across from the east.

Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen on Monday urged the EU to stop issuing tourist visas to Russians until the war ends.

“As long as Russia continues its invasion, Russian citizens should not be issued tourist visas,” she said, adding that it is “not right” for Russians to enjoy Europe’s freedoms “while their country bombs the homes of Ukrainians”.

Valtonen noted that Schengen countries granted nearly half a million tourist visas to Russians in 2025. Finland banned such visas in 2022, and she argued the rest of the bloc should follow suit.

news.originalContent:
The state-level announcement mirrors a federal indictment from May as the US steps up pressure on the Cuban government.

Florida, in the southeastern United States, has issued an arrest warrant for 95-year-old former Cuban leader Raul Castro.

The move comes as US authorities step up pressure on the government in Havana.

State Attorney General James Uthmeier said on Monday that the warrant was based on criminal charges over Castro’s alleged role in ordering two unarmed aircraft to be shot down in 1996.

The aircraft were affiliated with Brothers to the Rescue, a Florida-based group that helps Cubans fleeing the country. Four people were killed in the attack.

Castro faces state-level charges of conspiracy to commit first-degree murder in Florida.

“Raul Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,” Uthmeier wrote in a news release.

He said the arrest warrant was necessary accountability for the lives lost. “Thirty years later, we are still fighting for justice for Carlos Costa, Pablo Morales, Mario de la Pena, and Armando Alejandre Jr.”

The decision to shoot down the two small twin-engine planes has been the subject of renewed controversy over the last year, as Republican President Donald Trump seeks to oust Cuba’s communist leaders.

The attack took place on February 24, 1996. US authorities say the planes were flying over international waters and received no warning before they were shot down.

Cuban officials, meanwhile, have argued that previous Brothers to the Rescue flights had breached the country’s airspace, despite warnings to stay away.

Castro, now 95 years old, was Cuba’s defence minister at the time of the attack. A key figure in the Communist Party of Cuba, he later became president of the island in 2008, replacing his brother, the late revolutionary leader Fidel Castro.

Though he retired from the presidency in 2018, Raul Castro and his family remain powerful figures in Cuba’s government.

Since the start of the year, the Trump administration has signalled it would like to see regime change in Cuba.

To trigger such change, the administration has tightened US restrictions on the island, including by imposing a de facto energy blockade in January.

By threatening steep tariffs against any country that supplies Cuba with oil, the US has effectively barred fuel exports to the country, according to experts.

That, in turn, has caused deteriorating conditions on the island and strained the country’s already meagre power system, which relies heavily on fossil fuels. Only 40 percent of Cuba’s oil is produced domestically.

Additional sanctions have been placed on Cuba’s economy, limiting its state-run industries.

But in May, the Trump administration unveiled a superseding indictment also targeting Raul Castro for the 1996 plane downings.

It charges Castro with federal crimes including conspiracy to kill US nationals, destroying aircraft and four counts of murder.

The Trump administration issued a statement in support of Florida’s actions against Castro on Monday.

“We’re committed to pursuing every lawful, prosecutable avenue to bring accountability, including parallel federal and state prosecutions,” US Attorney Jason Reding Quinones said.

“Our historic federal indictment laid the groundwork, and James [Uthmeier] and his team have now taken the important step of bringing charges under Florida law.”

Trump has previously used indictments to justify military operations targeting government leaders that are at odds with the US, including former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

news.originalContent:
(Illustration by Daily Caller Staff)

Take a dip in The Drain Pipe, your weekly guide to the Washington swamp.

Is it time to place the “swing voter” on the Endangered Species List?

When I volunteered as a precinct captain in Northern Virginia during the 2024 presidential election, I met voters of all kinds who were terrified of what the Biden-Harris administration was doing to our country and hopeful that electing Donald Trump would undo it. While I haven’t been a political operative in a while (and I don’t plan to be), it’s clear that the mood has changed.

Democrats only need three seats to flip the House, where sixteen Republican seats are toss-ups as of Oct. 16, according to the Cook Political Report. Meanwhile, they only need two seats to flip the Senate, where six Republican seats are reportedly toss-ups as of Oct. 6.

This doesn’t mean that Americans are “switching sides,” nearly as much as it could mean that they may feel that Trump hasn’t delivered the respite they were promised.

The share of Americans identifying as Republican fell 3% since last year (31% to 28%), while the share identifying as Democrats grew marginally by 1% (28% to 29%), according to data gathered by Pew Research Center from Jan. 30 through June 18. Meanwhile, those who identify with neither party rose 3% (41% to 44%).

Only 65% of Republicans say they’re certain they’ll vote in the midterms versus 72% of Democrats, according to an ABC/Post/Ipsos poll published Saturday night. The poll also found that Trump’s approval rating reached a record-low of 33%, with 75% of respondents rating America’s economy negatively.

These polls come as Trump urges voters to “pretend” he’s “on the ballot.” Sure, much of the inflation his administration is trying to tackle could’ve been caused by his predecessor, but the Iran War — which has reportedly cost the average American household $2,000 — may’ve made that a riskier request to make.

With Democrats repeatedly proving themselves to be the party of socialism and political persecution, it’s easy for Republicans to campaign on being the party of common sense. But that doesn’t mean that’ll be enough to cross the finish line. In order to meet Americans where they’re at — in the growing middle — Republicans’ receipts must show common good.

— Spencer Maximilian Lombardo

When I volunteered as a precinct captain in Northern Virginia during the 2024 presidential election, I met voters of all kinds who were terrified of what the Biden-Harris administration was doing to our country and hopeful that electing Donald Trump would undo it. While I haven’t been a political operative in a while (and I don’t plan to be), it’s clear that the mood has changed.

Democrats only need three seats to flip the House, where sixteen Republican seats are toss-ups as of Oct. 16, according to the Cook Political Report. Meanwhile, they only need two seats to flip the Senate, where six Republican seats are reportedly toss-ups as of Oct. 6.

This doesn’t mean that Americans are “switching sides,” nearly as much as it could mean that they may feel that Trump hasn’t delivered the respite they were promised.

The share of Americans identifying as Republican fell 3% since last year (31% to 28%), while the share identifying as Democrats grew marginally by 1% (28% to 29%), according to data gathered by Pew Research Center from Jan. 30 through June 18. Meanwhile, those who identify with neither party rose 3% (41% to 44%).

Only 65% of Republicans say they’re certain they’ll vote in the midterms versus 72% of Democrats, according to an ABC/Post/Ipsos poll published Saturday night. The poll also found that Trump’s approval rating reached a record-low of 33%, with 75% of respondents rating America’s economy negatively.

These polls come as Trump urges voters to “pretend” he’s “on the ballot.” Sure, much of the inflation his administration is trying to tackle could’ve been caused by his predecessor, but the Iran War — which has reportedly cost the average American household $2,000 — may’ve made that a riskier request to make.

With Democrats repeatedly proving themselves to be the party of socialism and political persecution, it’s easy for Republicans to campaign on being the party of common sense. But that doesn’t mean that’ll be enough to cross the finish line. In order to meet Americans where they’re at — in the growing middle — Republicans’ receipts must show common good.

About a month into the unrest sweeping France, rioters burned down the spire of Limoges’ 19-century city hall last Saturday. CBS News reported that French police arrested at least 1,800 people as between 550,000-800,000 people engaged in demonstrations across the nation.

Vice President JD Vance, in response to the arson, posted on X last Saturday that he “pray[s]” France will “stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn.”

“Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion,” he wrote. “They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn’t listen … And I hope Americans are paying attention. This is the future congressional Democrats seek for your country.”

Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn’t listen. I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn. And I hope Americans are paying attention. This is the future congressional Democrats seek for your country.

Trump has also attributed the violence to immigration.

“France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a Sunday morning Truth Social post. “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!”

However, multiple mainstream media outlets claim the riots started because of dissatisfaction over rising cost of living and poor conditions within schools. If that’s true, then this wouldn’t be the first time the Left used affordability as an excuse to destroy France.

Le jour d’après à Limoges. Désolation. Tristesse. Colère. https://t.co/lj5xHgTnB4

For roughly 1,300 years, France was a bastion of Christendom, being traditionally referred to as the “Eldest Daughter of the Church” since King Clovis I’s conversion to Catholicism in either 496 or 508. That streak ended after the French Revolution overthrew the monarchy and Church in 1789. That’s also when we got the labels “Right” and “Left.” The monarchists and clergy sat on the right-hand side of the legislature, while the atheistic revolutionaries sat on the left side.

What was the revolutionaries’ justification for overthrowing the French establishment and unleashing ten years of terror? Cost of living. So, one could conclude that leveraging affordability to justify destroying the West has always been the modus operandi of the French Left … and the American Left may be taking notes.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Herika Martinez / AFP via Getty Images)

American cattle producers are suffering “substantial economic losses” 30 days into President Donald Trump’s midterm gambit to lower the price of ground beef, according to a recent report from an agricultural industry watchdog group.

Trump announced in August that the U.S. would waive tariffs on ground beef imports from Argentina, allowing 300,000 metric tons of lean beef to flood the domestic market on the condition that it would be sold 25 percent below market prices. According to a new report from Farm Action, the move has had little positive effect for consumers but a major negative effect on ranchers and cattle producers. (RELATED: Does Something Smell Off About Trump’s Bulk Beef Buy?)

While American consumers have seen a 13-cent, or 2% reduction, in the price of ground beef since August, Farm Action found that the impact of the Trump administration’s policy on cattle producers has been “far more significant.”

“Since the policy took effect, prices paid for live and dressed cutter cows, which compete directly against the lean beef imports, have fallen 12.2 percent and 13.9 percent, respectively. These steep declines further squeeze ranchers’ profitability and discourage investment in rebuilding the nation’s cattle herd, which has fallen to historic lows,” says the report, which cites data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

Farm Action also noted that only “37.5% of the first 100,000-metric-ton tranche had entered the country” as of September, meaning 200,000 metric tons still need to be imported. (RELATED: Egg Price Fixing Shouldn’t Be Just Another Cost Of Doing Business)

“With two additional tranches authorized, cattle prices could face further downward pressure, threatening domestic production and increasing reliance on imported beef,” the report says. “So far, the policy has delivered minimal relief to consumers while inflicting damage on American cattle producers that could ultimately drive beef prices higher, instead of lower.”

Sarah Carden, senior director of research and policy at Farm Action, said in a press release that the data raises “serious questions” about whether the administration’s policy has already backfired.

“Ranchers are seeing steep declines in the prices they receive, and consumers still haven’t seen clear, meaningful relief at the grocery store. We can’t rebuild America’s cattle herd by undermining the producers who raise our cattle,” she said. “If the administration wants to make beef more affordable, it needs to address the lack of competition in the beef supply chain and invest in a stronger domestic cattle industry—not put the burden on American ranchers.”
